articles.body: El Real Oviedo ha dado este lunes uno de los golpes de timón más llamativos de la temporada en Segunda. Julián Calero ya no es el entrenador del equipo azul, y eso que venía de asaltar Cádiz con una victoria que devolvía a los asturianos a la pelea por el playoff. La propiedad mexicana no se ha conformado y ha apostado por un nombre de impacto: Raúl González Blanco, que firma hasta junio de 2028 y se estrena por fin en un banquillo profesional. La decisión no se entiende sin las últimas semanas. El Oviedo cayó en la Copa del Rey ante el Numancia, de Segunda Federación, en la tanda de penaltis tras un 3-3 que desnudó sus problemas atrás, y después perdió 2-3 en el Carlos Tartiere contra Las Palmas. Ni el triunfo en el Carranza salvó a Calero. Raúl llega con seis temporadas en el Castilla, una Youth League conquistada en 2020 con el Juvenil A del Real Madrid y la etiqueta de técnico que gestiona bien vestuarios. Nunca ha dirigido a un primer equipo, y esa es la gran incógnita que pesa sobre la apuesta. Su estreno no será precisamente amable. Este fin de semana recibe al Girona en el Tartiere. El gran favorito para las casas de apuestas para levantar el título de LaLiga Hypermotion es el Almería, que se paga a 4,5 en Bet777. Los andaluces tienen la plantilla más profunda de la categoría y un fútbol de posesión muy pulido. Muy cerca aparece el Castellón, a 5. El conjunto de La Castalia es junto al Oviedo el equipo que más balón tiene en la categoría y ha confirmado que su proyecto va en serio. En un segundo escalón de las apuestas deportivas figura el Eibar, a 9, un clásico de Segunda que sabe competir en noviembre y en mayo, siempre sólido en Ipurua. A la misma cuota, 9, se paga el Granada, que alterna buenas tardes con tropiezos inesperados pero tiene pegada para engancharse a cualquier racha. El Mallorca, a 10, recién descendido, conserva una base de Primera y es de esos equipos que pueden despegar en la segunda vuelta. El Burgos, a 11, es la gran sorpresa de la tabla de cuotas: un equipo trabajado, fiable en El Plantío y con pocas concesiones defensivas. Y ojo al Girona, a 13, que además será el primer examen de Raúl. Un buen resultado del Oviedo ese día movería, y mucho, el mercado de ambos. El Oviedo se paga a 17, exactamente lo mismo que su eterno rival, el Sporting. Una cuota que implica algo menos de un 6% de opciones y que, de momento, no recoge el cambio de entrenador.

articles.title: Luka Doncic powers the Lakers past the Hawks, stretching the win streak to 6
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night.

Walker Kessler had 21 points and 10 rebounds, and Collin Sexton had 18 points and six assists off the bench.

The Lakers were without guard Austin Reeves, who missed the game due to illness one day after scoring 43 points at Detroit.

Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 23 points and was 5 of 8 from 3-point range. The Lakers as a team shot 43% from beyond the arc (15 of 35).

CJ McCollum led the Hawks with 21 points off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 20 points and Oneka Okongwu had 16 for Atlanta, which saw its winning streak end at four games.

Dyson Daniels was the primary defender on Doncic, and he also had 10 points, eight assists, four steals and a rare 3-pointer.

The Hawks pulled cut the Lakers lead 115-111 on a Daniels bucket with 3:30 to play, but a 6-0 burst by the Los Angeles put the game out of reach. Doncic had a driving layup and an assist during the run.

The Lakers built a 20-point lead in the second quarter as they sliced through the Hawks defense repeatedly. Doncic set up teammates with eight first-half assists and Kessler had three easy alley-oop dunks off Sexton drives to the basket. The Hawks recovered late in the half with some improved shooting and cut the deficit to nine at the break.

Lakers rookie Cameron Carr had a two-handed dunk in transition in the first quarter for his first career points.

Lakers: At Milwaukee on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Collins puts up 24 points and 10 rebounds as Pistons beat Davis and Wizards, 122-111
articles.summary: DETROIT (AP) — John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena.The Pi...
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena.

The Pistons overcame a 44-point, 13-rebound performance from Anthony Davis, who had been a game-time decision because of an ankle issue.

Daniss Jenkins finished with 22 points and eight assists after moving into the starting lineup. Jenkins scored a career-high 31 points in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers. Duncan Robinson scored 22 for Detroit.

AJ Dybantsa scored 21 points for Washington, which lost its fourth straight. Trae Young had 20 points and seven assists.

The Pistons led by 10 at the half and shot 63.2% from the floor in the third quarter. Jenkins had 13 points in the quarter as Detroit extended the lead to 103-87.

Cade Cunningham didn't return until midway through the fourth quarter after picking up a fifth personal foul in the third, but the Pistons had built a comfortable 115-99 lead.

Davis, who set the scoring record at the Palace of Auburn Hills with a career-high 59 points for the Pelicans in 2016, started the game like he was headed toward breaking Anthony Edwards' Little Caesars Arena record of 53.

He finished with 30 points in the first half on 10 of 11 shooting — making both of his 3-point attempts and 8 of 9 attempts from the free-throw line.

But he didn't get much help. Young scored 13 points in the half, but the other three starters combined for 14 points and the bench added just one point.

Meanwhile, the Pistons had three starters in double figures — Robinson, Collins and Cunningham — and got 19 points from the reserves.

Wizards: At Indiana on Wednesday before hosting Detroit on Thursday.

Pistons: At the Washington on Thursday. ___

articles.title: When Is Quentin Grimes Coming Back? Lakers Announce Positive Injury Update
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers announced a Quentin Grimes injury update after the wing was listed as 'out' for Monday following a right finger sprain. The post When...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are without wing Quentin Grimes for the team's game against the Atlanta Hawks, as the free-agent addition suffered a finger injury in the Sunday night win over the Detroit Pistons. While there were initial concerns that Grimes' injury could cause a long-term absence, according to the latest updates, the Lakers aren't expecting him to miss a ton of time.

Grimes signed a four-year, $60 million deal with Los Angeles over the summer to become the team's fourth-highest-paid player. While he hasn't had a great start to the year, the Lakers would prefer him to be healthy and available on a nightly basis.

After Grimes suffered his finger injury in the Lakers' win over the Pistons, X-rays returned negative, and though he was ruled out for the team's Monday night game, the latest updates should signal good news for Los Angeles.

When Is Quentin Grimes Coming Back? Lakers Announce Positive Injury Update

For now, it is uncertain when Grimes will return from his injury for the Lakers. However, ahead of the team's game against the Hawks, head coach JJ Redick offered a positive update on his status.

"No worries," Redick said, per team reporter Benjamin Royer . "Just some swelling…So I think just being cautious with it, and hopefully he's back, you know, the next game or so."

Grimes went down with the finger injury on Sunday, leaving the game after scoring 12 points and dishing out four assists in 33 minutes.

"Quentin Grimes just went back to the Lakers locker room with a member of the medical staff," ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported.

After that win, Grimes had an X-ray on his finger, which came back negative. It was good news for a Lakers team that still needs all the help it can get out of its wings this season.

"Grimes banged a finger on his R hand, per the Lakers. X-rays taken at the arena came back negative," McMenamin added in a subsequent Grimes injury update.

Despite the positive injury news, Grimes was still listed on the Lakers' injury report as out for the game against the Hawks.

He is officially listed as 'out' due to a right finger sprain, but as Redick said in his latest Grimes injury update, it doesn't look like the player will be out for an extended period.

The Lakers have been cautious with other injuries so far this season, so it makes sense the team is playing the long game amid the hot start to the year.

Los Angeles' Key Free Agent Addition So Far This Season

As mentioned, Grimes signed with the Lakers for $60 million to become the fourth-highest-paid player on the team, only behind Luka Doncic , Austin Reaves , and Walker Kessler on the franchise's salary cap.

Before the season, there was an expectation he'd be the starting small forward, but so far this year, that's only been the case on one occasion when Doncic was sitting out. Instead, Matisse Thybulle , Ziaire Williams , and Jake LaRavia have all been the different starting forwards for the Purple and Gold, even though each is making significantly less money than the 26-year-old.

It's been a bit of a down campaign for Grimes so far, as through 11 games, Grimes is averaging eight points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.5 assists on 43.1/25.6/68.8 shooting splits in 25.9 minutes per appearance.

With his latest injury, this is the first game of the year Grimes has missed. However, as Redick said in his update on the wing, it doesn't look like he'll miss much time. Though Grimes hasn't necessarily been as advertised for the Lakers so far, he remains a key piece in the rotation, regardless of what his poor numbers might show.

Along with missing Grimes due to injury, Los Angeles is without Reaves on Monday night, as he sat out with an illness.

The next chance for both to return is in the team's next game on Wednesday, as the Lakers continue a four-game road trip to play the Milwaukee Bucks .

articles.title: Bills injury update: Is Dalton Kincaid playing in Week 9?
articles.summary: Dalton Kincaid will be helping the Bills against the Vikings in Week 9.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will host the Buffalo Bills in primetime in Week 9 as they play each other with a lot on the line. The Vikings lost their undefeated record in Week 8 to the Detroit Lions , so they will be looking to get back on track against arguably the best team in the NFL.

Both teams are dealing with a handful of injuries that could swing the matchup in one team's favor or the other. In this piece, we are discussing the status of Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid.

Kincaid has been active for Week 9 against the Bills. Through three quarters, he has been held to just two catches for 23 yards. Josh Allen always has his eyes on his security blanket, though, so he could make an impact at any time.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving combine for 78 points, erase 13-point Pacers lead in 125-122 Mavs' win
articles.summary: Pascal Siakam has monster first half but Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving were too much in a 125-122 Mavericks win over the Pacers
articles.body:
See the best photos from Pacers vs Mavericks

DALLAS -- Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving exploded for a combined 78 points to erase a 13-point Pacers lead and give the Mavericks a 125-122 win at the American Airlines Center on Monday night.

The Pacers fell to 3-8 with their second straight loss. The Mavericks improved to 7-4.

Flagg posted 43 points on 16 of 25 shooting, grabbed 10 rebounds and dished out six assists. Irving scored 35 points and hit on 7 of 10 3-pointers. Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 29 points, 26 coming in the first half. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points, cener Ivica Zubac had 16 points. Kelly Oubre Jr. had 14.

Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving go berserk on Pacers

The Pacers corrected a lot of their problems from Saturday's loss to the Nuggets. They had a much stronger first-half performance. They shared the ball, shot it reasonably well and fought on the defensive end. But they simply had no antidote for one of the most potent starting backcourts in the NBA on a night when both of its members were sizzling.

Irving and Flagg, both former No. 1 picks out of Duke, hit inferno levels against the Pacers and produced more than half of the Mavericks' total production. They combined for 78 points on 27 of 43 shooting including 10 of 16 from 3-point range.

Flagg, the 6-9 wing functioning as a shooting guard -- and a great one -- scored 43 points on 16 of 25 shooting, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range, and also hit 8 of 8 free throws. He added 10 rebounds and dished out six assists. Irving, the 15-year veteran and nine-time All-Star, had a vintage performance that showed little evidence of his ACL tear last year. He finished with 35 points on 11 of 18 shooting including a shimmering 7 of 10 from 3-point range.

The Pacers hung around long enough to have a chance in the final minute, but late buckets by Flagg put the game away. He answered three Aaron Nesmith foul shots with a critical jumper to put the Mavericks up four with 1:02 to play. Then after a Nesmith 3-pointer, he hit a jumper on offensive rebound by Naji Marshall off Marshall's own missed free throw to put the Mavs up three with 26 seconds left. Two key free throws by Irving helped the Mavericks put the game away.

Pascal Siakam brilliant in first half, swarmed in second

With Tyrese Haliburton still out, the Pacers have been in need of something next level from Siakam to carry the squad. He's been solid throughout the Pacers' tough start and entered Monday averaging 21.4 points per game on 51.7% shooting, but he hadn't scored 30 points since the season opening win over the Pelicans and had only surpassed 25 points twice all season. It was even more imperative because they were up against Irving and Flagg.

Siakam certainly gave the Pacers everything they could have asked for in the first half. He hit his first eight field goals and his first five 3-pointers before finally missing a heat-check 3 in the final minutes of the second quarter. At the break he had 26 points on 8 of 9 shooting, six rebounds, four assists, no turnovers and no fouls, posting a +15 plus-minus figure in just 16 minutes of game action. In the second half, however he was swarmed with constant double and triple teams and scored just three points on 1 of 7 shooting.

Kelly Oubre Jr. gives one of his best efforts

The Pacers have been waiting for a breakout game from off-season free-agent signing Kelly Oubre Jr. as he entered Monday's game averaging just 8.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, shooting 41% from the floor and just over 23% from 3-point range. There's still certainly another level the Pacers would still like to see, but Monday's performance was a step in the right direction on both ends.

The long-armed 6-8 wing scored 14 points on 6 of 9 shooting including 1 of 3 from 3-point range. He had two rebounds but also gave the Pacers a defensive option off the bench they could use on Irving, Flagg and others.

Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Pacers Insider newsletter .

articles.title: Dhinidhi Desinghu puts celebrations on hold, eyes LA Olympics
articles.summary: BENGALURU: India’s teenage swimming sensation Dhinidhi Desinghu returned from Dakar, Senegal, on Monday morning to a warm welcome from officials of the
articles.body: BENGALURU: India’s teenage swimming sensation Dhinidhi Desinghu returned from Dakar, Senegal, on Monday morning to a warm welcome from officials of the Karnataka Swimming Association. After a traditional reception, she was felicitated at her home club, Dolphin Aquatics, at the Centre of Excellence (CoE).But after winning two landmark bronze medals at the Youth Olympics last week, celebrations were not high on the 15-year-old Bengaluru swimmer’s agenda. Her books were waiting.Although her parents urged her to take a day off and enjoy the Deepavali festivities, Dhinidhi wasted little time getting back to her studies and private tutorials. With her Class XI examinations at Kendriya Vidyalaya, DRDO, beginning on Nov 16, academics have taken priority once again.For the teenager, the discipline that has helped her make a mark in the swimming pool extends to the classroom too.“There is no time to celebrate because my examinations are coming up. I carried my books to Dakar also, but didn’t want to add to the stress and didn’t study,” said the teenager who won gold, silver and bronze in 200m, 100m and 400m freestyle events respectively at the Asian Age Group Championships in Bangkok in July this year.Her coach, Nihar Ameen, who was delighted by his ward’s success, told TOI, “She’s a talent we all know that—more than that, she is a hard worker. Talent alone doesn’t give you the results. At some point in time, you’ve got to break through the glass ceiling. And you’ve got to really work hard and only then go to the next level, and that’s what she’s doing.”Dhinindhi, who was the youngest in India’s Paris Olympics contingent, won the 100m freestyle bronze with a national record time of 56.27 seconds and finished the 200m freestyle event in 2:02.28 for the bronze medal.While the results are promising, Ameen said they are looking ahead to attaining the ‘A’ qualifying mark for the 2028 LA Olympics.“Much of the last couple of years we’ve been trying to get her to get to the point where she breaks two minutes and works towards the A qualifying time for the LA Olympics (1.56.43). It’s a Herculean task, but I’m glad she is ending the season on a high, you know,” stated the Dhronacharya awardee.While none of the female swimmers attained the qualifying mark set by the Swimming Federation of India for the recently concluded Asian Games, Ameen believes swimmers like Dhindhi should have been given an opportunity to compete against the best in Asia.“The best of the country need to be motivated. If our youngsters see that there are no swimmers (female) going to the Asian Games, Olympics or the Commonwealth Games, why would they stay in the course till they peak when they are 19 or 20 years old? The best in the country should have been sent, even for representation; on that count, I feel the federation made a grave error, and it impacted Dhinidhi psychologically,” pointed out Ameen.For Dhinidhi, the target is clear: qualifying for the LA Games.“My goal is to qualify for the Olympics. We are already towards the end of 2026, and the qualifiers start next year, so there isn’t much time. It is very difficult to qualify in the 100 and 200 metres freestyle events, but I will give my best,” she said.But for the next couple of weeks, the focus is on academics and not timing in the pool.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cricket Australia will not open another investigation into ‘sandpapergate’
articles.summary: ‘We’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation,’ Cricket Australia chief says after Khawaja’s revelations.
articles.body:
The top cricket official in Australia has ruled out another investigation into the so-called “sandpapergate” scandal despite remarks by Usman Khawaja and David Warner that knowledge of the 2018 ball-tampering plot was widespread throughout the team.

Cricket Australia (CA) ⁠boss Todd Greenberg said on Tuesday he believed all players held “very different views” from Khawaja’s version of events of the 2018 tour of South Africa as described in his recently released autobiography.

“There are specific details in his ⁠book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others,” Greenberg told ⁠local radio station SEN.

“But we have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received,” he added.

“That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that. We don’t see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again. I don’t think ‌there’s anything that can be gained from that.”

CA imposed bans and other penalties on Warner, former captain Steve Smith and former Test batter Cameron Bancroft four days after the incident came to light during the Cape Town Test.

Khawaja, in extracts from his autobiography published in Australian media, said “open, lighthearted discussions” were held during the South Africa series about ways to scuff up the ball, including by using sandpaper.

He said discussion of tampering was not confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.

“It was all of us,” Khawaja said in the book, ⁠according to Australian media.

Warner, who retired from international cricket more than two years ago, ⁠broke his silence about the incident on Monday to throw his support behind Khawaja .

In a video posted on social media, Warner described his former teammate’s account as 100 percent accurate and the CA investigation as “botched” and “rushed”.

The four Australian bowlers who played in the Cape Town Test in 2018 and continue to represent the nation – Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon – issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any knowledge of the plot.

Captain Cummins said in South ‌Africa last month that he had spoken to Khawaja about his autobiography and was not concerned about any potential fallout.

“Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then,” he said.

Some commentators have questioned why Khawaja ‌waited ‌eight years to speak out and accused him of trying to boost sales of his book Sabr.

Khawaja responded on social media on Tuesday, saying he had no commercial motives.

“I’m very fortunate, I don’t need the money,” he said.

articles.title: Meet Stephanie Case - the first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
articles.summary: Stephanie Case makes history by becoming the first woman to complete extreme 100-mile race in Antarctica.
articles.body:
Ultra-runner Stephanie Case has made history by becoming the first woman to complete an extreme 100-mile race in Antarctica.

The Antarctic Ice Ultra consists of 38 loops of a 4.2km course in the Schirmacher Oasis in Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica.

The 43-year-old ran alongside penguins and battled severe wind and temperatures as low as -35C - the coldest organisers have ever seen - to cross the finish line in second place overall in a time of 17 hours 31 minutes and 39 seconds.

Due to the harsh weather conditions, the race was brought forward to start at 1am on Sunday morning and Case says it was as much about survival as performance.

"When you're out in that environment for 20 minutes it's OK but when you're out in it for 17 hours or more, it can take a huge toll on the body because you have to expend so much energy just to keep yourself warm," Case told BBC Sport.

"The thing is that you need to run fast, but you need to do it in a way that you don't sweat, because if you sweat, that's a killer. It will make you cold instantly."

'Going to the bathroom was a real challenge'

Such is the brutal nature of the challenge on a continent that has 24/7 daylight, very few people attempt it each year and even fewer finish. This year, only four of the eight runners that started the 100-mile race crossed the finish line.

Previously only ever attempted by men, Case was one of three women on the start line but the Canadian was the only one to finish.

One of the challenges Case had not considered though, as a self-declared "mountain goat", was managing toilet breaks in the extreme temperatures.

"On a trail you could normally just go in the woods, but due to bio-security reasons, you can't leave any trace in Antarctica. And then going to the bathroom, when you are wearing so many layers and taking off your gloves for even five seconds can put your hands at risk of frostbite, it was a real challenge," she said.

"The environment is so harsh, and things can go wrong so quickly… It was just relief when I crossed the finish line that I'd actually done it and in a time that I was super proud of. It was just an outpouring of emotion."

The human rights lawyer crossed the line 29 minutes after Chinese runner Yusheng Ni, who smashed his own world record - set last year - by over five and a half hours.

Alongside making history, Case had also been chasing the world record but knew she would have a "formidable challenge" on her hands with Ni, who has completed more than 500 ultramarathons, in the pack.

"There were parts where I was 60 seconds behind him or I was sometimes just 200 metres behind him. It was a real race. But whenever he saw me getting close, he would look behind and he would just take off. I think we really pushed each other to get our best performances. I feel super proud of what I was able to do," she said.

Case went viral last year for breastfeeding her baby daughter Pepper during her victory at an ultramarathon in Snowdonia.

While the response was largely positive, she says some of the backlash she received is what inspired her to take on this challenge to show "motherhood is not the finish line". To do it in a place that has historically been described as the "womanless continent", she says, is a fitting achievement.

"I know that when I'm going out and doing the things that make me feel happy and whole, it makes me a better mum and I can come home and and show my daughter all the things that she might want to do and all the things that are possible for women," Case said.

"I felt like the best way to clap back at anyone who thought that I should be at home with my baby was to go to the most extreme place on Earth and try to get the record."

articles.title: Luka Doncic’s 32 points help Lakers beat Hawks; Wembanyama powers Spurs
articles.summary: Doncic has been averaging 40 points per game this season with the Lakers on top of the NBA Western Conference.
articles.body:
Luka Doncic has scored 32 points as the in-form Los Angeles Lakers have rolled to a sixth straight victory with a 124-114 defeat of the Atlanta Hawks in the NBA.

Doncic, whose sensational early-season form has propelled the Lakers to the top of the Western Conference, once again led from the front on Monday to secure an impressive win on the road.

The Slovenian star finished with 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks in a dominant all-around performance.

Doncic, who is averaging 40 points per game this season, received offensive support from Sandro Mamukelashvili, who delivered an eye-catching 23 points from the bench, including five three-pointers.

Walker Kessler added 21 points. Collin Sexton scored 18 and Ziaire Williams 12.

Lakers coach JJ Redick paid tribute to the contributions of Doncic, Sexton and Mamukelashvili on a night when the team were missing Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (injury).

“I thought Collin did a really nice job of giving us some juice, and Sandro had his best game as a Laker,” Redick said. “That was awesome.”

“Luka, again, just orchestrating. He was out there without a secondary ball handler, so he had to be on the ball a lot, and that was taxing. I thought he handled it well,” Redick added.

The Lakers improved to 10-2 at the top of the Western Conference as Atlanta fell to 7-5.

The San Antonio Spurs, meanwhile, maintained their hot pursuit of the Lakers in the West, extending their winning streak to nine games after blowing out the Phoenix Suns 122-96 on the road to improve to 9-2.

Spurs star Victor Wembanyama – fresh from a career-high 52-point performance last week – was once again in dazzling form, dropping 40 points with 11 rebounds, eight blocks and three assists in a dominant victory.

“There’s a lot of good going on, obviously,” San Antonio coach Mitch Johnson said of Wembanyama’s rich vein of recent form.

“I think he’s allowing the game to unfold naturally, and he’s doing a great job of putting himself in positions to take advantage of the opportunities that are in front of him. And his teammates are doing a good job of utilising him when appropriate.”

The Golden State Warriors kept their own winning streak alive on Monday, thrashing the New Orleans Pelicans 138-87 to record their eighth consecutive victory.

Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski scored 25 points apiece while rookie sensation Yaxel Lendeborg added 23 as the Warriors improved to 8-3.

In other games on Monday, the Detroit Pistons improved to 7-3 with a 122-111 defeat of the Washington Wizards after 24 points from John Collins.

The Memphis Grizzlies are also on 7-3 after their 118-102 victory over the Toronto Raptors. The Cleveland Cavaliers, meanwhile, stumbled to a 124-112 loss to the Charlotte Hornets.

In Houston, Jamal Murray scored 38 points for the Denver Nuggets, but it was not enough to stop the Rockets from claiming a 110-100 victory.

Kevin Durant scored 23 points, and Alperen Sengun added 20 as the Rockets halted their two-game losing streak.

articles.title: Jimmy Butler hilariously cosplays as Warriors coach during Pelicans game
articles.summary: Jimmy Butler may be out for a few more months as he recovers from a torn ACL, but he’s trying to make an impact for the Golden State Warriors however he can....
articles.body:
Jimmy Butler may be out for a few more months as he recovers from a torn ACL, but he's trying to make an impact for the Golden State Warriors however he can. And in signature Butler fashion , he finds a way to be hilarious while doing so.

Butler was on the Warriors' bench during their 138-87 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night. But he wasn't just in simple street clothes. The injured star forward decided to dress up in full coaching staff cosplay complete with a clipboard prop, all while offering advice and encouragement to his teammates.

One can just see that the vibes in the Warriors locker room are immaculate, and that Butler is still well involved in his team even though he can't suit up yet for his team on the hardwood.

Whatever Butler was doing for the team on Monday certainly worked. The Warriors demolished the Pelicans by 51 points, and they have now won eight consecutive games to move to 8-3 on the new campaign.

It looked like everything was turning bleak for the Warriors after they lost three consecutive games to start the season. Moreover, Kristaps Porzingis' injury and eventual decision to step away from the game made it so that the Dubs' big-money signing this offseason won't be able to contribute to the team this season.

But the Warriors have figured it out, with Stephen Curry playing at an elite level, and the Dubs' youngsters, such as Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski, have been brilliant for the team during their eight-game winning streak.

They are certainly buying enough time for Butler to return, and rumor has it that the Warriors forward is actually ahead of schedule in his recovery. It looks like the Warriors have one last hurrah in them, and it's as much as Curry deserves after staying committed to the franchise.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Schedule, new format, players, prize money, past winners as Luke Littler looks to retain title
articles.summary: Everything you need to know including new format, expanded field, prize pot, players, and past winners ahead of the Grand Slam of Darts 2026; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
The Grand Slam will see an expanded field of 48 players battle it out for a whopping £1,000,000 in prize money and the Eric Bristow Trophy, all live on Sky Sports .

The competition starts this Saturday November 14 and will run until Sunday November 22. The quarter-finals will take place on November 20 and 21, before the semi-finals on the afternoon of Sunday November 22 ahead of the final in the evening.

GROUP A (1) Luke Littler, Niels Zonneveld, Beau Greaves

GROUP B (16) Jermaine Wattimena, Alan Soutar, Lisa Ashton

GROUP C (8) Josh Rock, Kevin Doets, Tommy Morris

GROUP D (9) Stephen Bunting, Cameron Menzies, Raymond Smith

GROUP E (4) Gerwyn Price, Sebastian Bialecki, Joe Hunt

GROUP F (13) Ryan Searle, Andrew Gilding, Charlie Manby

GROUP G (5) Jonny Clayton, Rob Cross, Anton Ostlund

GROUP H (12) Wessel Nijman, Niko Springer, Adam Sevada

GROUP I (2) Luke Humphries, Joe Cullen, Paolo Nebrida

GROUP J (15) Luke Woodhouse, Krzysztof Ratajski, Tom Sykes

GROUP K (7) James Wade, Ricky Evans, Cam Crabtree

GROUP L (10) Michael van Gerwen, Jeffrey de Graaf, Henry Coates

GROUP M (3) Gian van Veen, Bradley Brooks, Carl Sneyd

GROUP N (14) Chris Dobey, Martin Schindler, Jan Schmidt

GROUP O (6) Ross Smith, Gabriel Clemens, Rusty-Jake Rodriguez

GROUP P (11) Nathan Aspinall, Karel Sedlacek, Maik Kuivenhoven

Instead of eight groups of four, the expanded 48-player field is now split into 16 groups of three.

Rather than the top two in each group progressing like in previous editions, only the top player from each group will progress.

That means each player only has two group stage matches rather than three, so every match will carry A LOT of weight.

Effectively, each group is a round-robin format.

In the group stage, two points will be awarded for a win, and no points are awarded for a defeat.

Should there be a three-way points tie in any group after the round-robin games have been played, these would be split as follows:

Total leg difference Total legs won Total legs won against throw Highest total tournament average (to two decimal places) Highest winning match average (to two decimal places)

If players cannot be split after the above criteria, a play-off will be organised between the players at the end of the session in which the final group game is played and will be a two or three-way nine-dart shootout in which the player scoring the most points is deemed the winner.

The order of throw would be determined by PDC ranking, with the highest ranked player having the option to throw first, second, or third.

Following the completion of the Group Stage, each group winner will progress to the knockout stage from the last 16 onwards, and the tournament will proceed in bracket order as follows:

When and where is the Grand Slam of Darts?

The event takes place from Saturday November 14 through until Sunday November 22, live on Sky Sports .

The tournament is held at the WV Active Aldersley, Wolverhampton, with bumper crowds expected at every session.

Last year, Luke Littler came through with a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries to go back-to-back in the major. In 2026, he will be going for his third Grand Slam title in a row.

The money has gone up! The prize pot has increased from £650,000 in 2025 to a whopping £1,000,000 in 2026 thanks to the expanded field.

It means that the winner of the major will now take home £200,000, the runner-up clinching £100,000.

The semi-finalists will secure £60,000 and the quarter-finalists will leave Wolverhampton with £35,000.

If you make it to the last 16, £20,000 is the prize, while finishing second in a group means £12,500.

If you finish bottom in your group, you leave with £5,000.

Littler is the most recent winner in 2024 and 2025, with Humphries claiming glory before him in 2023.

Michael Smith ended his PDC major jinx in 2022 as he held the Eric Bristow Trophy aloft following his convincing 16-5 win over Nathan Aspinall.

Since 2007, there have been just nine different winners of the Grand Slam of Darts. Phil Taylor is the most successful in the tournament with six victories, Van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price in joint second with three apiece.

Littler could join that list with a third win in three straight years.

Although there have only been eight winners, 19 different players have competed in the final with the likes of James Wade, Peter Wright and Anderson unable to pick up the trophy. Martin Lukeman was the latest to join that list in 2024.

Luke Humphries became the seventh player to throw a nine-darter in Grand Slam of Darts history during his victory over Michael Smith in Group A back in 2025.

Humphries took out 144 to complete his third nine-darter of 2025 and wrap up a 5-3 victory, his second win of the tournament, with the 'perfect leg' the first at the event since Ryan Searle hit a nine-darter to win his Group D match against Nathan Rafferty in 2023.

The first came from Wade back in 2008, with Josh Rock, Dmitri Van den Bergh, Dave Chisnall and Kim Huybrechts the others to do so. No player has previously fired a nine-dart leg at the Grand Slam of Darts and gone on to win the tournament that same year.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Pipi Estrada, antes de entrar en ‘Gran Hermano VIP’: “Si voy con estrategia, la voy a cagar”
articles.standfirst: El periodista visitó por sorpresa Radio MARCA y contó cómo afronta su tercer reality tras ‘Supervivientes’ y ‘Pesadilla en el Paraíso’
articles.summary: El periodista visitó por sorpresa Radio MARCA y contó cómo afronta su tercer reality tras ‘Supervivientes’ y ‘Pesadilla en el Paraíso’
articles.body: Pipi Estrada apareció por sorpresa en el estudio de Radio MARCA para felicitar a Chitu por su cumpleaños y acabó contando cómo se prepara para entrar en ‘Gran Hermano VIP’. El periodista, que ya había hecho pública su participación, explicó que a sus 70 años vive la oportunidad como “un premio”. También admitió que lo que más le intriga es cómo se llevará con el resto de concursantes. “La convivencia es impredecible”, dijo. Estrada repasó su trayectoria antes de afrontar su tercer reality. Recordó que ha cubierto cinco Eurocopas y cinco Mundiales, que siguió al Real Madrid durante más de dos décadas y que ya pasó por ‘Supervivientes’ y ‘Pesadilla en el Paraíso’. “Voy con responsabilidad porque evidentemente no quiero defraudar”, explicó. Preguntado por si tiene pensado seguir alguna estrategia para durar más en el concurso, Pipi lo tuvo claro. “A un tigre no le puedes quitar las rayas. Si funciono con estrategia, la voy a cagar”. El periodista dijo que le va bien cuando va “de cara” y que, si hay desacuerdos en la casa, los afrontará con firmeza. También reconoció que, como amigo, debería “frenar la impulsividad” y que, como padre, a veces es demasiado protestón. En lo profesional, se quedó con la vocación y confesó que todavía le molesta mucho que se le escape una noticia. Antes de despedirse, Estrada contó que se iba a cenar una tortilla francesa. “Quiero entrar en la casa con tres kilos menos”, explicó. Su idea es llegar en forma a las pruebas y poder competir con los concursantes más jóvenes. Y por si llega la primera nominación, dejó un mensaje a los oyentes. “Que me votéis con V, no con B, no me deis la patada”.

articles.title: Paga 8,9 millones por un Ferrari de carreras que después no puede llevarse a su casa
articles.standfirst: El Ferrari 499P Modificata es una versión del prototipo que ha ganado tres veces seguidas las 24 Horas de Le Mans para multimillonarios que no son pilotos
articles.summary: El Ferrari 499P Modificata es una versión del prototipo que ha ganado tres veces seguidas las 24 Horas de Le Mans para multimillonarios que no son pilotos
articles.body: El Ferrari 499P Modificata es uno de los coches más inalcanzables que ha salido de Maranello en los últimos años, y lo decimos tanto en el sentido económico como en el de la velocidad. Pero seguro que no le parece tan inalcanzable al afortunado millonario que este pasado domingo ganó la puja celebrada en Ginebra y se ha hecho con él por 8,9 millones de euros. Suena a muchísimo, y más si tenemos en cuenta que no puede circular por carretera abierta (algo lógico) pero tampoco participar en carreras oficiales. Pero eso no quita que sea una máquina con tecnología propia de un coche ganador de las 24 Horas de Le Mans. ¿Qué tiene este Ferrari para justificar semejante precio? Para empezar, no se trata de un modelo de producción adaptado para rodar en circuito (hace décadas, eso ocurría), sino de la versión destinada a clientes privados del 499P con el que Ferrari regresó a la categoría reina de Le Mans en 2023, medio siglo después de su última participación en la carrera francesa. Aquel año logró la victoria y corroboró que Ferrari había hecho muy buen trabajo al repetir en 2024 (con el español Miguel Molina) y 2025. La 499P Modificata se presentó en 2023 como una variante de uso exclusivo en circuito, sin las limitaciones que imponen los reglamentos deportivos. De hecho, es incluso más potente que el coche que corrió en Le Mans. Combina un motor V6 de 3,0 litros biturbo, situado en posición central, con otro eléctrico de 272 CV que mueve el eje delantero. La potencia conjunta alcanza los 707 CV, pero basta pulsar un botón para activar la función Push to Pass y disponer de otros 163 CV (870 en total) durante un máximo de siete segundos. Hay otra diferencia importante respecto al 499P que compite en el Mundial de Resistencia, y es que, por reglamento, el sistema híbrido del coche de competición solo puede transmitir fuerza al eje delantero (además de al trasero) cuando supera los 190 km/h. La Modificata, sin embargo, dispone de tracción total desde cualquier velocidad. A ello se suma que monta neumáticos Pirelli específicos, con un compuesto derivado de la Fórmula 1, y cuenta con ajustes propios en la suspensión, la electrónica y la gestión del motor. Por si con tanta exclusividad no fuera suficiente, Ferrari creó en 2024 el programa Sport Prototipi Clienti para que los propietarios de la 499P Modificata pudieran disfrutar de sus bólidos en circuitos de todo el mundo. La marca se ocupa de la logística, el mantenimiento y la asistencia técnica en pista durante los encuentros (no se les puede llamar carreras) organizados para estos clientes, que se celebran junto a las actividades de F1 Clienti y el XX Programme. El millonario propietario de cada coche paga por los servicios y por participar en cada evento, pero no tiene que organizar por su cuenta el transporte del coche ni preocuparse de buscar mecánicos; tan solo, llega en su jet privado o helicóptero (o como quiera) a las inmediaciones del circuito y se dispone a disfrutar pilotando. La unidad subastada es un ejemplar de 2024, conserva su decoración roja original y apenas ha rodado más allá de las pruebas de puesta a punto realizadas por Ferrari, ya que su propietario no ha participado en ninguno de estos encuentros. Así que sospechamos que quizá fue el 'calentón' de un multimillonario al que después no le vino bien eso de darse un descanso para desfogarse en el circuito. Su nuevo dueño tampoco podrá llevárselo a casa de inmediato. Salvo sus salidas para participar en estos encuentros, el 499P Modificata debe permanecer en las instalaciones de Maranello hasta diciembre de 2028. Y esto es algo que, por ejemplo, no sucedía con los Ferrari de Fórmula 1 del programa Ferrari clienti, cuyos propietarios, si así lo deseaban, se podían llevar el coche a su casa. La subasta de Gooding Christie’s en Ginebra ha sido la primera ocasión en la que una 499P Modificata ha salido a la venta en una puja pública y las expectativas de precio se han superado. Lo cual demuestra que se ha abierto una nueva vía para los coleccionistas de coches más pudientes: la de los prototipos de resistencia que no están homologados para competir, pero que permiten experimentar en circuito la mejor tecnología de los ganadores de Le Mans.

articles.title: El Langui cierra una temporada inolvidable con una plata en Sao Paulo
articles.standfirst: El rapero y actor logró llegar a su primera final en una Copa del Mundo de boccia. Aún tiene opciones de ganar otra medalla por equipos
articles.summary: El rapero y actor logró llegar a su primera final en una Copa del Mundo de boccia. Aún tiene opciones de ganar otra medalla por equipos
articles.body: Juan Manuel Montilla, 'El Langui', cierra su segunda temporada en la boccia con otra medalla más. De todas las competiciones, sólo se le ha resistido el podio este año en el Mundial. En el resto, cuenta sus participaciones por medallas. En apenas dos temporadas practicando este deporte paralímpico ya tiene una colección. La última es la plata en BC1 la Copa del Mundo de Sao Paulo (Brasil). No fue la única medalla española, ya que Laura Utrero, en la modalidad BC3, también se colgó una plata. "Ha sido un campeonato brutal. De esos que, como deportista, te hacen crecer, aprender y darte cuenta de el camino que llevo recorrido", cuenta a MARCA. Era su primera final de una Copa del Mundo, donde se midió a deportistas que están entre los diez mejores del ranking mundial. El Langui fue 'in crescendo' a lo largo del campeonato gracias a que estuvo en todo momento "muy enfocado, muy concentrado, con las ideas claras y, sobre todo, con una templanza que voy adquiriendo gracias a la experiencia acumulada durante este año". Porque en su primera temporada, compitió en la liga autonómica y en el Campeonato de España, después ya llegarían las citas internacionales con la selección este año, disputando no sólo Challengers sino también Mundiales y esta Copa del Mundo. El Langui hace balance: "¡Llevo un año como internacional y ya son 6 medallas! Cuatro en individuales y dos en equipo. Una auténtica locura que me hace valorar todavía más todo el trabajo que hay detrás". En la Copa del Mundo de Sao Paulo superó la fase de grupos, la pool, ganando y clasificándose para cuartos de final, donde se enfrentó al peruano Roly Castro, un deportista con muchísima experiencia, con años de competición internacional y muchas Copas del Mundo a sus espaldas. Como él mismo explica, "un rival especialmente peligroso en el juego corto, a tres y cuatro metros, muy certero y con una gran capacidad para ejecutar aéreos, sacar bolas y desmontarte una jugada en cuestión de segundos" Pero Juan Antonio López Mera, el entrenador del Langui, y el deportista supieron leer su juego, mantener su estrategia y llevarse una victoria importantísima que les metía en semifinales. Ahí se medía al singapurense Jovin Tan, número tres del ranking mundial. Era un partido especial porque fue el jugador que le eliminó en el Mundial de Corea del Sur en agosto. Le tenía ganas deportivas, muchas ganas de volver a medirse con él. Pero el partido empezó con una dificultad añadida. Debido a la humedad de Brasil, una de las bolas se había hinchado y, durante el control previo en la cámara de llamadas, no superó la prueba de diámetro. Resultado: penalización y a disputar la semifinal con una bola menos. Ante la dificultad añadida, el Langui se creció. "Entré muy concentrado, con muchísimas ganas, midiendo los tiempos, controlando cada decisión y jugando de tú a tú. Los dos somos jugadores que nos sentimos cómodos en corto, así que fue una auténtica batalla estratégica, de precisión, control y cabeza", explica Y el resultado fue el billete a la final. En la final le esperaba Kuanysh Askarbekovun, de Kazajistán, un deportista muy joven, situado también entre los 15 mejores del mundo y con un nivel técnico extraordinario. "Un jugador que convive con una distonía, pero que ha trabajado muchísimo para desarrollar un juego tremendamente constructivo y preciso", nos cuenta. La final fue un tú a tú hasta el último parcial, pero esta vez no pudo superarle. "La plata para mí tiene un valor enorme. Porque más allá del metal, me quedo con lo que significa haber llegado hasta aquí. Con la evolución, con los rivales a los que he conseguido superar, con la experiencia adquirida y con la sensación de estar creciendo como deportista en cada competición. esta plata supone sumar unos puntos importantísimos para el ranking mundial, con la posibilidad de colocarme entre los diez mejores del mundo, a falta de confirmación oficial", reconoce. El madrileño, afincado en Málaga, sigue compaginando el "ajedrez de las bolas" con los rodajes y actuaciones con su grupo de música. "Y aun así, aquí estamos. Peleando, aprendiendo y disfrutando de este deporte que tanto me está dando", dice orgulloso. "No puedo estar más contento con la progresión. Porque cada entrenamiento, cada viaje, cada partido y cada experiencia tienen un objetivo que está ahí, en el horizonte: los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028. Queda muchísimo trabajo por delante, soy plenamente consciente, pero creo que estamos construyendo un camino muy bonito, paso a paso, y ganas de seguir aprendiendo", concluye.

articles.title: Esha Singh leads India to team gold as Manu Bhaker joins her in 25m pistol final at ISSF World Championships
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the ISSF World Championships on Tuesday as Esha Singh spearheaded the country's charge to the women's 25m
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the ISSF World Championships on Tuesday as Esha Singh spearheaded the country's charge to the women's 25m pistol team gold, while also qualifying for the individual final alongside double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker.Esha, one of India's leading pistol shooters, topped the Indian trio in the two-day qualification round with a score of 590. Manu contributed 587 and Divya Subbaraju added 584 as India aggregated 1761 to clinch the gold medal.South Korea finished second with 1748 to take silver, while Vietnam claimed bronze with a total of 1745.The team triumph was complemented by Esha and Manu securing places in the individual final, giving India a double chance to fight for another medal and a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Esha's strong comeback powers IndiaThe 21-year-old Esha finished third in the individual qualification standings with 590, behind Germany's Doreen Vennekamp, who topped the field with 592 to equal the Olympic record, and Hungary's Veronika Major, who shot 591.Esha produced an impressive recovery in Tuesday's Rapid round after managing 292 in Monday's Precision round. She shot series of 100, 98 and 100 to register 298 in the Rapid round and finish with an overall score of 590.Manu also bounced back after a modest 289 in the Precision round. The two-time Olympic medallist put together a series of 99, 99 and 100 in the Rapid round to finish sixth with 587 and secure her place among the eight finalists.Divya, meanwhile, narrowly missed out on the individual final, finishing 10th in the qualification standings with 584.India eye another Olympic quota placeThe individual final presents India with an opportunity to add to its tally of Olympic quota places. The three medallists in the event will secure quota places for their respective countries, meaning India could potentially claim two if both Esha and Manu finish on the podium.Jaypal Malviya has already opened India's account in the Olympic qualification race at the championships. He won silver in the men's 10m air pistol to become the country's first shooter to secure a quota place for the Los Angeles Games at the event.The women's 25m pistol team gold and the presence of two Indian shooters in the individual final provide a significant boost to India's campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: '55-45 for Javokhir Sindarov': Russian GM Peter Svidler gives World Chess C'ship challenger narrow edge over D Gukesh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler believes Javokhir Sindarov holds a slight advantage over reigning world champion D Gukesh ahead of their
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Russian Grandmaster Peter Svidler believes Javokhir Sindarov holds a slight advantage over reigning world champion D Gukesh ahead of their upcoming World Championship match but feels it would be unfair to give the Uzbek a significantly higher edge.Speaking to FIDE, Svidler gave Sindarov a 55-45 advantage, while stressing that Gukesh's experience and ability in the unique World Championship format should not be underestimated.“For this match, 60% [for Javokhir Sindarov] is already very high. Even with the kind of a year and a half Gukesh has had, I don’t think going higher than 55 is justifiable," Svidler said.“He’s still a very strong player, it’s still a very specific format. So, I’m kind of willing to go 55-45 for Sindarov, but I don’t think I’m willing to go higher."Gukesh, meanwhile, is gearing up for the biggest challenge of his career as he prepares to defend his world title against Sindarov in a 14-game classical chess match scheduled from November 24 to December 12 in Geneva, Switzerland.Gukesh aims to defend World Chess Championship titleThe 20-year-old Indian recently visited the famous Tirumala Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Andhra Pradesh to seek blessings ahead of the title defence. The visit came days after he also offered prayers at Neem Karoli Baba's ashram.The upcoming contest will be historic, with both players set to be 20 years old when the match begins, making it the youngest World Championship encounter in chess history.Gukesh made history in December 2024 when he defeated China's Ding Liren to become the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion at the age of 18 years, six months and 24 days. He also became only the second Indian, after Viswanathan Anand, to claim the prestigious title.The championship will feature a maximum of 14 classical games, with the first player to reach 7.5 points being crowned champion. If the scores are level at 7-7, the title will be decided through tiebreaks.The opening ceremony is scheduled for November 22, while the first classical game will be played on November 24 at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva. The final classical game is scheduled for December 11, with December 12 reserved for a possible tiebreak.The championship carries a total prize fund of $2.5 million, with each player receiving $200,000 for every game won and the remaining prize money to be shared equally.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Moroccan trio make African Player of Year shortlist as Salah absent
articles.summary: WAFCON winners Cameroon dominate women’s list after heroics from Monique Ngock, Michaely Bihina and Marie Ngah Manga.
articles.body:
Achraf Hakimi will hope to defend his title of African Footballer of the Year on December 2 as he leads a trio of Moroccan players on the shortlist, which does not feature Egyptian star and former winner Mohamed Salah.

Morocco captain Hakimi is joined by Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari on the 10-man shortlist released by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) last week.

The trio led Morocco to a controversial Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title in January. Although Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 after extra time in the final , Morocco were subsequently awarded the title after Senegal walked off the pitch over a disputed penalty. A decision on Senegal’s appeal over being stripped of the title will be made ⁠⁠at the end of ⁠⁠November.

The three players also helped Morocco reach the quarterfinals of the World Cup, where Saibari was the country’s top scorer with three goals while Hakimi scored one.

At the club level, Saibari shone with Bayern Munich after they signed him for a hefty 50-million-euro ($56m) transfer fee this summer while Diaz continued to prove his worth with Real Madrid.

Hakimi, meanwhile, helped Paris Saint-Germain to their second consecutive Champions League title.

In 2025, he became the first Moroccan since 1998 and the first defender since 1973 to win Africa’s most prestigious award, finishing ahead of Salah and Nigeria striker Victor Osimhen, the 2023 winner.

The other players on the African Footballer of the Year shortlist are Amad Diallo (Ivory Coast); Yoane Wissa (Democratic Republic of the Congo); Antoine Semenyo (Ghana); Ismaila Sarr, Pape Gueye and Sadio Mane (Senegal); and Teboho Mokoena (South Africa).

Salah’s absence from the list has raised eyebrows because the Egyptian forward is widely recognised as a generational talent and one of Africa’s top players.

The former Liverpool star, now with the Turkish side Trabzonspor, took home the award in 2017 and 2018. Mane won the subsequent two awards.

World Cup heroics reflected in nominations

Notable names in the coach category are Egypt’s Hossam Hassan, who was subsequently sacked by the national team over a marital scandal, and DR Congo’s Sebastien Desabre, both of whom led their side to historic runs to the World Cup round of 16.

The Moroccan duo of Mohamed Ouahbi, who led the team during the World Cup, and Walid Regragui, who was the coach during qualification, were also nominated for their country’s success at the tournament while Cabo Verde’s coach Pedro Leitao Brito has made the shortlist for helping the island nation make its World Cup debut.

Goalkeeper Vonzinha, who became an overnight global sensation due to his World Cup heroics, is among the 10 nominees for goalkeeper of the year alongside Egyptian pair El-Mahdi Soliman and Mostafa Shobeir.

Morocco’s Yassine Bonou remains a leading contender after his performances at the World Cup and AFCON.

The World Cup also saw several young stars shine on the international stage, earning them places on the shortlist for Young Player of the Year. Ghana midfielder Caleb Yirenky scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner against Panama in the Black Stars’ opening match while Morocco’s Ayoub Bouaddi starred as a breakout defensive midfielder.

Bouaddi became the first African teenager to make five World Cup appearances and was signed by Manchester City in August. He is accompanied by compatriot Abdellah Ouazane on the shortlist.

Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) winners Cameroon have dominated every award category on the women’s side.

Midfielder Monique Ngock, 22, was named player of the tournament while Michaely Bihina was recognised as best goalkeeper. Marie Ngah Manga scored twice in Cameroon’s 3-0 final victory over Malawi.

Her brace tied her for most goals at a WAFCON (five) alongside Zambia’s Barbra Banda, 2024 winner of CAF Women’s Footballer of the Year, and Malawi’s Temwa Chawinga. All three along with Chawinga’s sister Tabitha feature on this year’s shortlist.

South Africa’s Thembi Kgatlana, who scored four WAFCON goals, is also a top contender for the accolade.

Standing out in the goalkeeper shortlist is Cameroon’s Michaely Bihina, who won the Golden Glove at WAFCON, and Malawi’s Mercy Sikelo.

Competition is also stiff for the women’s Young Player of the Year, which includes Cameroon’s Maeva Nyadjou, a breakout defender at the tournament.

Malawi’s Rose Kadzere scored in her side’s quarterfinal victory over Ghana to reach the semis and help secure qualification for the women’s World Cup.

articles.title: Pablo Torre says NCAA has no transgender athletes, conveniently leaves out the reason why
articles.summary: Rachel Maddow and Pablo Torre claim the trans athletes in women's sports debate is manufactured, ignoring the NCAA rule change that followed Trump's order.
articles.body: Pablo Torre and Rachel Maddow would like you to believe the controversy surrounding biological males competing in women's sports is a manufactured political issue. Never mind the female athletes who have lost championships, podium finishes and opportunities to biological males. We're supposed to forget all of that ever happened. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE During an appearance on "Pablo Torre Finds Out," Maddow accused Republicans of inventing a problem that has "literally no contact with the real lives of 99.9999% of Americans." Torre, meanwhile, offered what he apparently considered a compelling piece of evidence. "We called the NCAA and we said, 'Hey, how many trans athletes are competing in women's sports, or at all?' And the NCAA told us there are effectively zero. They can't find them." Great point, Pablo. Except you forgot to mention there's a reason for that. CARTON RIPS INTO PHILADELPHIA EAGLES HEAD COACH NICK SIRIANNI, SAYS HE COACHED HIS EVER GAME IN PHILADELPHIA - LISTEN NOW Biological males are no longer permitted to compete in NCAA women's sports On Feb. 5, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order titled "Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports," directing federal agencies to enforce sex-based athletic protections under Title IX. The very next day, the NCAA announced an immediate change to its transgender-athlete participation policy, restricting women's competition to "student-athletes assigned female at birth." The NCAA didn't even pretend the timing was a coincidence. "President Trump's order provides a clear, national standard," NCAA President Charlie Baker said in the Feb. 6 announcement. In other words, the rule was changed to address the very issue Torre and Maddow now suggest was never a real problem in the first place. And before that policy change, we have plenty of examples. Of course, there’s Lia Thomas — the University of Pennsylvania swimmer who previously competed on the men's team went on to win the 2022 NCAA Division I women's 500-yard freestyle national championship, beating Olympic silver medalist Emma Weyant. TRANSGENDER ATHLETES HAVE TAKEN 2,293 CHAMPIONSHIP SPOTS FROM BIOLOGICAL WOMEN, NEW RESEARCH FINDS Or CeCe Telfer, who previously competed in men's track at Franklin Pierce University before winning the 2019 NCAA Division II women's 400-meter hurdles national championship. Then there's Sadie Schreiner, who won the 2024 Liberty League women's 200- and 400-meter outdoor titles while competing for Rochester Institute of Technology, setting a conference record in the latter event. And OutKick has reported extensively on Blaire Fleming, the San Jose State volleyball player whose participation became the center of a national controversy in 2024. Fleming earned All-Mountain West honorable mention honors that season, while multiple opposing teams forfeited matches rather than compete against the Spartans. Those are just a handful of the documented examples. And they all happened before the NCAA changed its rules. You can debate whether those previous policies were fair or unfair if you want to. But pretending the controversy sprang from absolutely nothing requires ignoring years of actual, recorded events. And using today's participation numbers without acknowledging that the eligibility rules have changed? That's a pretty convenient omission. Torre wanted to deliver a "gotcha" by calling the NCAA and reporting that it couldn't identify transgender athletes currently competing. But if you're going to use the apparent absence of something as proof that it was never a problem, you should probably mention the rule that now prohibits it.
