articles.title: WWE's Big Mistake With 946, Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker's DQ Woes and More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: With Crown Jewel behind WWE, the focus for the November 9 edition of Raw on Netflix turned to Survivor Series where WarGames will return after Roman Reigns called for war between The Bloodline and 946.
articles.body:
With Crown Jewel behind WWE, the focus for the November 9 edition of Raw on Netflix turned to Survivor Series where WarGames will return after Roman Reigns called for war between The Bloodline and 946.

Jade Cargill, Michin and B-Fab also found allies in Fatal Influence to fight Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley and Bayley, setting the stage for a second WarGames to be announced soon.

Cody Rhodes and Rey Mysterio continued to fill out their teams for Team Mexico and Team USA, recruiting CM Punk, Je'Von Evans and Penta.

This was not the most exciting night of Raw but did set the stage for what fans can expect going into WarGames season.

What WarGames Can Learn From AEW's Blood & Guts

Last week, All Elite Wrestling completed its yearly Blood & Guts event, delivering two bloody and violent WarGames matches of their own.

While the level of gore on this show will never be a possibility for WWE, the two matches did show signs of what recent WarGames matches have lacked.

Each match was distinctive and memorable, elevating the talent involved while ramping up key stories on the roster, even though both matches were thrown together quickly into the show.

Strong physicality in the cage is also essential to selling any WarGames match. The point of this match is to sell that the two teams want to genuinely hurt each other to end their conflict.

Too often Survivor Series: WarGames has seen basic cage matches between teams that are simply hoping to win on a premium live event stage, which could be accomplished in a traditional Survivor Series match instead.

No one should pull their punches or hold back their weapon usage. Fans should be able to hear the impact of the offense, focused more on the intensity of the action than the high-flying finish expected of modern WarGames.

Even if Iyo Sky joins the latest women's WarGames, she should focus on selling the action not waiting for her turn to jump off the cage inside a trash can again.

Between The Bloodline and 946, the winning team should be the one that physical overwhelms the other, not the one that sets up the other on a table faster for a top-of-the-cage splash.

Moments are important for a big contest like this, but the focus should be stories that sell why WarGames is the most dangerous structure in WWE.

Stop Booking DQ Finishes for Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker

Twice now, WWE has booked Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker, only to deliver a disqualification finish.

No matter how good the action, a non-finish sells the match as non-essential, and WWE should not be delivered non-essential matches between two of its biggest rising stars.

It makes sense to protect both men given their importance to the future of WWE, but that is why this match should not be booked in the first place.

The next time Oba and Breakker fight, it should be a major PLE stage for major stakes. Anything less is a waste of a future headliner feud for WWE.

It's Already Clear That Team Mexico Must Beat Team USA in Traditional Survivor Series Match

It is nice to finally see the traditional Survivor Series elimination match back for the show that made that match type special.

There was a time that the traditional Survivor Series match was as important as the Royal Rumble match for continuing major feuds in WWE.

That time has likely passed for good, but Team USA vs. Team Mexico could be a fun exhibition match that will deliver great action involving major stars.

The problem is that Team USA already looks far more stacked than Team Mexico.

Rey Mysterio is a legend, but WWE has booked both Cody Rhodes and CM Punk as bigger stars than him in recent years.

Penta is the biggest name Mysterio could add for Team Mexico, and it seems likely Mysterio will fill out the remaining three spots with Rey Fénix, Dragon Lee and El Grande Americano.

Meanwhile, Rhodes will likely look to Trick Williams and Chad Gable to fill out the team, even look to a returning Seth Rollins.

The teams are not stacked evenly, but that should not stop WWE from elevating the talent of Team Mexico by giving them a definitive victory.

Penta or Americano as the sole survivor for Team Mexico would mean so much more than Trick or The Young OG standing tall for Team USA.

Survivor Series Match Card Predictions 🔮

"All Ego" Ethan Page is already showing his value as Intercontinental champion, delivering a memorable heel promo while establishing three great future challengers: Rey Fénix, Chad Gable and Big Cass.

However, all his work meant little when 946 took out all three men following their No. 1 contender match to sell that they were only stand-ins for The Bloodline later.

Fénix's win was immediately rendered pointless next to the story that WWE cares more about, and it is unlikely WWE will ever let these men get revenge.

It is especially confusing for the heel stable to take down the disliked heel Cass, making him into an example for 946's strength.

Nothing was accomplished in this segment that was not already set up in previous weeks or delivered in the main event finish of the night.

Meanwhile, three of WWE's most reliable recent midcard stars were made into fodder for an already established heel team that barely wrestles.

Every year, WWE has delivered both a men's and women's WarGames match for equal representation, but the actual story builds have never looked equal.

While the men always have clear stable warfare at the center of the conflict, the women's WarGames has lacked clearly defined teams, instead throwing together faces and heels at the last minute.

This year may have the laziest set-up yet as Jade Cargill, B-Fab and Michin have somehow aligned with Fatal Influence just in time for WarGames to beat up a collection of babyfaces they don't like.

Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley had to awkwardly add Bayley to their ranks from Raw and are still down at least one woman for WarGames.

Whether they add Paige, Iyo Sky, Stephanie Vaquer, Chelsea Green or Sol Ruca, none of them were involved in this rivalry until the moment they are thrown into the mix.

Since the men's WarGames match is the central story of Raw, the women's WarGames match should be the central story of SmackDown, but it is nowhere close.

It has nothing to do with either women's world championship, instead focused purely on Women's Tag Team Championships that have not been on an ESPN+ PLE since WrestleMania 42.

The women's WarGames match is an insulting placeholder for serious storytelling in WWE's women's division.

articles.title: 9 NHL Injuries That Have Hurt Teams So Far
articles.summary: Injuries are a fact of life in the NHL and if your favorite team can avoid serious ones, you're living well (and lucky). While some injuries can be upsetting for a little while, others can completely upend an entire season.
articles.body:
Injuries are a fact of life in the NHL and if your favorite team can avoid serious ones, you're living well (and lucky). While some injuries can be upsetting for a little while, others can completely upend an entire season.

We're still early enough in the NHL season, but with U.S. Thanksgiving approaching and how teams that aren't in playoff positions by then tend to have a harder go of things the rest of the season, any team dealing with a star player being out of action with an injury is really bad news. We hate to see anyone get hurt, but when the league's best players are sidelined, it's even more painful that we don't get to watch them dazzle us with their abilities.

We'll be taking a look around the league at some of the biggest names who have been KO'd by maladies and how much that's hurt how those teams are faring to this point in the season.

After going without captain Aleksander Barkov for all of last season, seeing Barkov go down with an injury in the second game of this season rightfully had everyone in South Florida nervous. Fortunately, his latest injury isn't a season-ender, and he should be back in the coming weeks, but the Panthers have been without him and Brad Marchand and it's tested their depth in a difficult way.

Although going without Marchand is tough, Barkov does everything for Florida. He's an elite scorer, defender and leader by example in the room. Even though their lineup is distinctly veteran, they've got their share of hot-tempered vets in Matthew and Brady Tkachuk as well as Radko Gudas. Having Barkov there to keep everyone focused goes a very long way as evidenced by their back-to-back Stanley Cups.

At 9-7-2, the Panthers are holding it down and in the middle of the pack in a brutally competitive Atlantic Division. If they can keep it level until Barkov (and Marchand) return, things will get a lot tougher for everyone else when they do.

The Wild are sitting atop the Central Division and it's pretty incredible that they are given they've been without defenseman Brock Faber all season. Faber fractured his skull when he was hit by a shot in preseason and needed surgery to fix things up.

A scary injury like that is reason enough to hold your breath, but with Faber back skating again and eager to get back on the ice, the way Minnesota has made things work without him is worthy of applause. Yes, having Quinn Hughes as the No. 1 defenseman helps, but with captain Jared Spurgeon and other veterans like Jonas Brodin and Olli Määttä, it makes life on the blue line a little easier to handle without Faber.

Faber is arguably the biggest absence to the Wild lineup, but they've been without goalie Filip Gustavsson after recovering from offseason surgery as well as both Nick and Marcus Foligno. There's no doubt, however, that when Faber returns, they're going to be that much better.

Seeing any player get hurt is hard to watch, but when Igor Shesterkin went down after a collision with the post while making a play, seeing him in so much obvious pain had all of us hoping for the best but thinking the worst. When it was confirmed that the Rangers superstar goalie was done for the season after just five games, especially after just scoring his first NHL goal, it was gut-wrenching.

Shesterkin is an entertaining goalie to watch and when he's on, there are few better than him in the league. The Rangers having to scramble to make do without him, especially while also losing Joonas Korpisalo at the same time, delivered a harsh blow to their hopes of getting back to the playoffs.

Rookie Dylan Garand has hung in there as the de facto No. 1. Meanwhile, veteran James Reimer came and went as did farmhand veteran Spencer Martin. Now with Korpisalo back, that'll give Garand a chance to breathe, but knowing they're without Shesterkin for the season puts the Rangers firmly in the rumor mill for any goalies who could be had, especially on a short-term or expiring contract. Still, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan which means they're in the race and that's more than a lot of people expected after watching Igor go out.

Ranking NHL's Most Frustrated Fanbases for 2026-27

Terrible Contracts Teams Wish They Could Dump 🤦‍♂️

The Islanders were some folks dark horse team to make the playoffs this season and Mat Barzal's knee injury that's kept him out from Day 1 this season helped put a damper on those thoughts.

Barzal is getting close to returning. He's been skating and joined the team on a recent road trip, but going without a star talent like him still hurts. The Isles are 7-6-3 which isn't bad but isn't great either because they're in the muddled middle of the pack in the East, but their forward group is screaming out for help and Barzal's return will be a huge help.

Bo Horvat is the team's leading scorer and defenseman Matthew Schaefer is doing a lot of everything from the blue line to make things go. Veteran Brayden Schenn is producing, but beyond him the rest of the scoring is coming from younger guys like Simon Holmstrom, Victor Eklund and Emil Heineman. No doubt that when Barzal returns it'll give them a much-needed boost whether he's playing center or wing.

Throughout his career with the Winnipeg Jets, defenseman Josh Morrissey has been one of their best and steadiest players by way of the quality of his play and the fact he would stay healthy over the past few years. But this season, an upper-body injury has kept him off the ice more often than on it.

In four games, Morrissey has no goals and three assists. Without their No. 1 defenseman, the Jets have had their ups and downs already this year what with a long losing streak and now a three-game win streak heading into a matchup with the Devils who won't be starting Morrissey's former teammate Connor Hellebuyck.

Whoever is in goal for the Jets is certainly better off with Morrissey handling the puck and slowing down opposing forwards, but being without him for 14 games already has really hurt them regardless. The Jets lack high-end defensive depth and how good Morrissey is gets lost often because he's in Winnipeg.

The Canadiens are 11-3-3 to start the season so it would be hard to know if they were missing anyone from the lineup, but one key guy they've gone without is forward Ivan Demidov.

Demidov is an offensive driver and power play demon for Montréal and in two games this season he has a goal and an assist and, strangely enough, his injury occurred during the preseason, but he tried to tough it out. Doing that may have inadvertently extended the 2-4-week prognosis the Canadiens initially announced and he's remained out of action.

While we're sure Habs fans have nitpicks about how they've played and made note of areas they could be better if Demidov were healthy, the Canadiens are rolling to start the year. They'll undoubtedly be that much better when Demidov returns and get the guy who put up 19 goals and 43 assists (62 points) in his rookie season a year ago.

As far as first seasons with a new team who you just signed a massive contract extension with go, this one has been a nightmare for Bo Byram in Chicago.

Byram is currently out of action with an upper-body injury, one which his agent Darren Ferris said he wants Byram to see a specialist for. This came after playing in six games for the Blackhawks in which he had no goals and an assist as well as a minus-7 plus-minus rating.

Slow starts in new places happen and Byram is a good enough player to let his play do the talking eventually. But with his mysterious injury and Chicago off to yet another horrendous start to the season, Byram's time to rewrite the story will have to wait and it's unfortunate because his style of play would at least give the 'Hawks some life to the United Center and give it some much-needed added excitement.

The rough start the Philadelphia Flyers have gotten out to has been hindered in part thanks to being without leading scorer Travis Konecny for a chunk of time.

Konecny has played in nine games this season and has a goal and four assists. While his absence allowed rookie Cole Knuble an opportunity, having Konecny in the lineup makes the Flyers a better and more frustrating team to play against and those are two things they have not been so often this year.

Konecny led the Flyers in scoring last season with 68 points including 27 goals. He's got a star player's contract, and he's committed to playing in Philly with a full no-move clause, so even if things get tougher for the Flyers, he's not going anywhere unless he says he will. Fortunately for Philly, Trevor Zegras is playing well, and Matvei Michkov is scoring goals (he has 10 already). With a healthy Konecny back, they have to believe things will turn around... or else.

Back in 2023-2024, Thatcher Demko was one of the best goalies in the NHL and helped lead the Vancouver Canucks to the playoffs. In the three seasons now since then, he's played 43 games and has yet to hit the ice this season. It's perhaps not a coincidence that the Canucks have missed the playoffs and sunk to the bottom of the Western Conference in that time.

All right, so that's not all on Demko's injury-ridden seasons, but not having an elite No. 1 goalie for 75 percent of the games is a major obstacle to overcome and Vancouver hasn't been able to get around it at all. The Canucks are off to a rough start again this season and going with Kevin Lankinen (for the third straight season) and Leevi Merilainen instead hasn't been the same as having a healthy Demko.

Demko is slowly working his way back and while no news isn't exactly good news, Canucks coach Manny Malhotra isn't counting him out for this season. We're all hoping to see him back because when he's healthy and he's on, he's phenomenal.

articles.title: Ranking the NHL's 8 Most Frustrated Fanbases for the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Sports fandom tends to be more about frustration than celebration. Only one team is winning a championship each season, and they are typically rare events that you get to experience maybe once every couple of decades. Anything more than that is insanely lucky. For the fanbases that do not get to experience that, there is going to be a wide range of disappointment.
articles.body:
Sports fandom tends to be more about frustration than celebration. Only one team is winning a championship each season, and they are typically rare events that you get to experience maybe once every couple of decades. Anything more than that is insanely lucky. For the fanbases that do not get to experience that, there is going to be a wide range of disappointment.

Especially if it is a team that has not won, or been close to winning, for several years.

So let;s take a look at some of the most frustrated fanbases in the NHL right now.

It is not necessarily about just having a bad team this season. It is also about how long it has been since the team has had any success, how bleak the long-term outlook might be, and any other number of variables that can go into frustration.

If you're a team that's won a championship in the past 10 years or so, you don't really get to claim the most frustrated label. So, for as bad as things are for the Chicago Blackhawks are right now? You're not that far removed from winning multiple Stanley Cups. You are not going to be on top of the list. Same thing applies to the Pittsburgh Penguins. You might be bad now, but you were really, really good very recently. It is just your time to be bad. Sometimes it happens.

There are a lot of other fanbases that do not have that experience. Let's talk about them.

You can have SOME frustration if you are Blackhawks fan. But you do not get to go to the top of the list. You do not get to tell everybody how bad you have it.

As bad as things have been lately, you are not that far removed from three Stanley Cups in six years. That still carries a lot of weight, and while it does not give the current organization a free pass, it does take some of the sting away for the fans.

Having said that, this organization is a mess, the rebuild looks failed, and they are still the worst team in hockey. They are worse now, in year four of Connor Bedard's career, than they were the year before they drafted him. Nobody seems to have any idea what they are doing here, and it might only get worse if they start making more desperation roster moves.

The Jets have been reasonably successful in recent years, and are not that far removed from a Presidents' Trophy. But so much of their success has had a little bit of a smoke-and-mirrors element to it given how goalie dependent it has been and the lack of urgency from the front office.

The general manager (Kevin Cheveldayoff) doesn't make trades unless he is forced into it.

The drafting and player development has not been great.

So much of the success that they have had has been the result of Connor Hellebuyck hiding a lot of their flaws and simply being one of the best goalies in the world for more than a decade. And even then, he had a habit of underperforming in the playoffs, and then forced his way out this this season, resulting in the trade to the New Jersey Devils. It just seems like his entire tenure here was mostly wasted, and now they have to pick up the pieces after he forced his way out and try to rebuild a team that is not largely goalie dependent. Do they have the right people in charge to do that? Recent history does not paint a promising picture for it.

Their surprising trip to the 2025-25 playoffs, and a series win over their arch-rivals, the Pittsburgh Penguins, was a nice temporary distraction from the mediocrity that has been the better part of the past 12 years.

And then they have followed it up with an absolutely brutal start to the 2026-27 season that has seen them play a painfully boring brand of hockey, take a step backwards in pretty much every aspect of the game, and watch as some of their young players (Matvei Michkov, Porter Martone) play through some truly puzzling usage.

Even worse, the front office basically told fans over the summer that a step backwards is something they were prepared for, while they seemed to have no other plan for the offseason except to hope that the Anaheim Ducks did not match their Leo Carlsson offer sheet (they did).

There are worse situations in the NHL. But that does not mean this is not a frustrating existence at the moment.

Injuries That Have Hurt NHL Teams So Far

Terrible Contracts Teams Wish They Could Dump 🤦‍♂️

The Sabres did make the playoffs a year ago, and they did win a round. So they have that going for them. In doing so, they were very close to a trip to the Eastern Conference Finals, and while they were a potential regression candidate this season (and still are) it is still a pretty good young team with a lot of talent.

But this is still a franchise that is just one year removed from a 14-year playoff drought, which is the longest playoff drought in NHL history.

I would also argue that there was plenty to be frustrated about coming into this season, even after last year's playoff appearance, because they did nothing to add to the roster and only subtracted from it in the short-term. While getting the No. 4 overall pick for defenseman Bowen Byram was a sensible move and great value, it still took away a top-four defenseman without another one coming in.

The 2025-26 season gave everybody a little excitement, and it gave ownership a temporary break from rightfully angry fan. But it is still a fanbase that has to be immensely frustrated with where the franchise has been over the past 15 years. The jury is still very much out on where it is going this season.

It's been a long time since this franchise was consistently competitive, and it's probably going to be a bit longer before it is given the current state of its rebuild.

Even worse, it's just not a very entertaining team at the moment. Bad and boring is no way to go through an 84-game NHL season. The most entertaining thing about the Flames right now is whenever goalie Devin Cooley talks after games.

Let's also not lose sight of the fact that after acquiring Jonathan Huberdeau as part of the Matthew Tkachuk trade, he immediately ceased to be productive and will likely never play like a star ever again. Tkachuk, meanwhile, is one of the best players in the league and the focal point of a team that won back-to-back Stanley Cups.

You do not have to be that old to have a memory of the Red Wings being a model NHL franchise and one of the most successful teams in pro sports. But time is starting to pass quickly, and the grace period that being a championship level team brings is beyond its shelf life.

It has been 18 years since their most recent Stanley Cup Final appearance and 19 years since their last championship. It has also been a literal decade since their last playoff appearance and 13 years since their last playoff series win.

The lack of results for more than a decade is a problem.

Where the problem gets worse is the entire organization looks like a rudderless ship with incompetent ownership and zero direction.

The Steve Yzerman era ended in July, but they do not have a full-time general manager to replace him.

Their captain and longest-tenured player, Dylan Larkin, wants a trade and is not playing for the team.

Simon Edvinsson, one of their best young players, remains unsigned as a restricted free agent and would reportedly prefer a trade as well.

The team is still decidedly average and looks to be on the verge of an 11th consecutive non-playoff season.

This is a mess. But not quite the biggest mess. You could be under the age of 20 and still probably have some memory of a reasonably successful team.

The Canucks have made the playoffs just three times in the past 13 years, and are coming off a 2025-26 season that saw them finish with the worst record in the NHL by a substantial margin. It was during that season that they had trade one of the best players the franchise has ever seen in defenseman Quinn Hughes because they knew he was not going to re-sign there.

And then they lost the NHL Draft Lottery and fell down to the No. 3 overall pick, missing out on the chance to get both Gavin McKenna and Ivar Stenberg.

It leaves the Canucks as a franchise that has never won a Stanley Cup, and also never picked first in the NHL Draft.

If nothing else, maybe they can change the latter part this year because they are, once again, on track to finish with the worst record in the NHL with just three wins in their first 20 games.

It's just been a directionless team for more than a decade now, and now that they are clearly rebuilding it looks like it is going to take a long time to get back to respectability.

At least this particular version doesn't have the drama that followed the 2024-25 team around with the beef between J.T. Miller and Elias Pettersson, while the latter saw all of his offensive creativity and skill seemingly disappear under former head coach Rick Tocchet. It has been a bad team. It has been a dysfunctional team. It has been a directionless team. It has been everything you do not want a professional sports franchise to be.

There might not be a more underrated fanbase in the NHL than the one that resides in Columbus.

These people have been given a non-stop circus, and they still do a reasonably good job filling their building and creating a strong atmosphere.

They deserve better than what they have been given by this franchise.

Just think about everything this team has put its fans through since entering the league, and especially recently.

They have never appeared in a Stanley Cup Final.

They have never won the Presidents' Trophy.

They have never finished higher than third place(!!) in their division.

They have made the playoffs just six times in their first 25 years.

They have made it through to the second round just one time.

They have not made the playoffs in six years, and could be working on a seventh-consecutive season on the outside.

They are on their sixth different head coach since the start of the 2020-21 season, including the embarrassing Mike Babcock failure.

They missed playoffs a year ago with an almost impossible collapse over the final weeks of the regular season.

They have consistently been ditched by high-profile players, including this season when Kirill Marchenko made it clear he would not re-sign there and ended up getting traded to the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Their best player, and the reigning Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, has been the subject of rumors regarding his long-term future.

As if all of that is not enough, they are off to one of the worst starts in the league this season.

Other than all of that, everything here is great.

If you are still loyal through all of that, you are a real one. And also probably incredibly frustrated.

articles.title: BOBBY BURACK: Dianna Russini wants sympathy without accountability in Mike Vrabel scandal
articles.summary: Dianna Russini joins BetUS for a new weekly podcast but still dodges key questions about the Mike Vrabel photos and The Athletic ethics breach.
articles.body: Dianna Russini announced Monday that she will return to media with a podcast for offshore gambling company BetUS. In her first interview since resigning from The Athletic in April, Russini delivered two messages. First, her new show, "The Russini Report," will air each Wednesday. Second, she is a victim of "heartbreaking" lies. Let's focus on that second point. CRAIG CARTON ISSUES AN APOLOGY TO ANGEL REESE, "I MISS YOU!" - DOWNLOAD NOW "The best way to describe what the last six months were like for me is heartbreaking," Russini told People. "At the beginning of this, it was a nightmare." "The lies became so out of control," she continued. "This was a runaway train, and there was nothing I could do to stop it. Once [my husband and I] realized nothing was going to stop this, it became unhealthy for us to read it because it wasn’t helping us heal. It was piling on and adding to what we were already dealing with." What lies? Who told them? What is the truth? Russini's account omitted answers to all three questions. Instead, she offered an appeal for sympathy and avoided any accountability. For someone whose job relies on providing inside information to the public, that's a damning response to a seven-month-long scandal. At a minimum, Russini violated her former employer's ethical standards. The Athletic said so in August. "Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic’s standards," Mike Semel of The Athletic said after an investigation into her reporting. "Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed." That assessment leaves no room for dispute. BOBBY BURACK: RYAN CLARK CLAIMS ESPN INTERVIEWED SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ABOUT TRANS ATHLETES TO IMPRESS OUTKICK In April, Page Six published photos in April showing Russini alone with Vrabel at an adults-only resort in Arizona. She claimed, a day after the report, that they happened to run into each other while she was on a hiking trip with female friends. Russini could have substantiated her explanation by providing photos from the supposed "girls' trip." She didn't. She seemingly wants us to accept that she participated in the first-ever girls' trip that didn't produce a single photo. Not one. After the initial report, various outlets obtained other photos of Russini with Vrabel over the course of at least seven years, dating to her time as an NFL reporter for ESPN. Notably, TMZ reportedly obtained documents showing that Russini and Vrabel rented a private boat together in Tennessee in June 2021. Russini was around seven months pregnant with her first child at the time. Maybe there is an innocent explanation for all this. It's hard to imagine, but we cannot say for certain. The optics are troubling. In any event, Russini asks that you, please, focus on her denunciation of the coverage instead. "When the Page Six item first appeared, The Athletic supported me unequivocally, expressed confidence in my work and pride in my journalism. For that I am grateful. In the days that followed, unfortunately, commentators in various media have engaged in self-feeding speculation that is simply unmoored from the facts," Russini said in her resignation letter. "Moreover, this media frenzy is hurtling forward without regard for the review process The Athletic is trying to complete. It continues to escalate, fueled by repeated leaks, and I have no interest in submitting to a public inquiry." The media did not place her at the resort with Vrabel earlier this year or at their other encounters over the years. She did that. The media also didn't escalate the scandal through a series of strange responses. The first came just a week after the initial report, when someone leaked to Page Six that Russini had saved a car crash victim. The headline: "Dianna Russini mounts daring rescue of elderly man, dog trapped in car crash a week after Mike Vrabel scandal." The unusual story attempted to cast Russini as a heroine to an old man and his dog. Unsurprisingly, it did not improve the public's increasingly contemptuous view of her. Presumably, the free edition of ChatGPT could have offered better advice than she received from those around her, including her CAA agent, Matt Olson. She has since hired a high-priced crisis manager, Melissa Nathan, who repped Blake Lively. Based on the People interview, her new approach isn't much better. In the interview, Russini came across as ignorant, if not delusional. From the beginning, she has conducted herself as if she could outsmart the rest of us. So far, it hasn't worked. The fact that not a single notable woman in sports media publicly defended Russini during the scandal underscores that. Whatever unnamed "lies" she speaks of – and maybe there are some out there on Reddit – they are not the reason she had to leave a premier job and resort to working with a gambling company that is not licensed in a single U.S. state. She is the reason she had to do that. The photos of her cozying up with Vrabel at the resort while reporting on his team's interest in AJ Brown are not a lie. The photos of her kissing Vrabel six years ago in New York City aren't either. Nor was the boating trip. Neither were the reports she published at The Athletic about Vrabel, without disclosing her relationship with him, romantic or not. Russini isn't the victim of lies. She's a victim of her own arrogance. Her arrogance is why she thought she could abandon boundaries with a head coach in the first place. Her latest insistence on portraying herself solely as a victim has compounded the damage. Her refusal to address the obvious has only deepened suspicions. She now says she plans to become a role model for other women. "I really hope that I can be someone other women see: you can pick yourself up, get back in there and not be afraid," she told People. "Because if you just do the work — and I hope to continue working at a high level — that’s all that’s going to matter. And I hope that quiets the noise." In actuality, Russini offered female reporters a cautionary tale about how not to cover the NFL. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Russini opened the promotion for her new project by saying she spent "20 years chasing the stories everyone is talking about." And yet, the story everyone is still talking about is the one she hopes a plea for sympathy will quiet.

articles.title: Liverpool captain leaves future open as contract expiry draws closer
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk ‘not in any panic’ over Liverpool contract and futureVirgil van Dijk remains calm about his Liverpool future despite approaching the final mo...
articles.body:
Virgil van Dijk 'not in any panic' over Liverpool contract and future

Virgil van Dijk remains calm about his Liverpool future despite approaching the final months of his contract without a decision on what comes next.

The captain's agreement expires at the end of June, leaving Liverpool with another significant discussion over one of their most influential players. Yet Van Dijk's response suggests he feels no immediate pressure to settle the matter.

Speaking after the victory over Crystal Palace, in comments reported by Gregg Evans for The Athletic , the 35-year-old made clear that he intends to continue playing. Whether that means another season at Anfield remains unresolved.

Van Dijk offered neither a promise to stay nor an indication that he has decided to leave.

"I want to keep playing and continue what I'm doing so let's see what the season brings," he said.

"I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else. There's nothing to report at the moment but that doesn't mean that there's any stress or anything."

His comments acknowledge both possible outcomes without suggesting that either is imminent. Discussions are expected in the coming weeks and months, according to The Athletic, but there is no agreement to announce.

"I feel good but it's not about me at the moment. I'm not in any panic whatsoever," he added.

For Liverpool supporters, that leaves uncertainty. For the player himself, it appears to be a situation he is comfortable allowing to develop while concentrating on his football.

Premier League availability strengthens his case

Van Dijk has played every minute of Liverpool's Premier League campaign, maintaining a central role while helping Jeremy Jacquet settle into the defence.

That availability gives the contract discussion a practical foundation. Liverpool are assessing a captain who continues to shoulder substantial responsibility, both through his own performances and his influence on a new teammate.

His contribution is not confined to experience accumulated in previous seasons. He remains an active part of the team's development under Andoni Iraola.

However, deciding on an extension requires looking beyond what a player is delivering today. Liverpool must also assess whether that level can be sustained throughout another agreement.

At 35, Van Dijk's age inevitably forms part of that judgement. It does not, on its own, provide an answer.

Fitness concern prompts Netherlands withdrawal

Van Dijk also revealed that his recent availability has come despite some physical discomfort.

"Mentally I'm in a good place, physically I've been struggling with a little niggle the last couple of weeks but I do everything in my power to be out there," he said.

He has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad for the international break, giving him time away from international fixtures.

The report does not identify the precise nature of the problem or establish a longer-term absence. It would therefore be premature to treat the withdrawal as evidence of a major fitness concern.

Nevertheless, managing his workload remains relevant to Liverpool's planning. His commitment to playing is clear, but preserving his effectiveness requires balancing that desire with the demands of a crowded schedule.

Defensive uncertainty adds weight to Liverpool decision

Van Dijk's situation sits within a broader set of questions about Liverpool's defence.

Joe Gomez is also approaching the end of his contract in June, while Giovanni Leoni remains sidelined as he recovers from an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Those circumstances strengthen the argument for continuity, although they do not guarantee that Liverpool will offer their captain fresh terms.

Van Dijk last extended his contract in April 2025, agreeing a two-year deal shortly before his previous arrangement expired. That history offers a reminder that an unresolved position during the season does not necessarily lead to a departure.

The current decision must still be judged on its own merits. Liverpool need to consider performance, availability and the balance of their defensive options.

Van Dijk has made his position clear enough: he wants to keep playing, appreciates what he has experienced at Anfield and is prepared for either outcome. The next step is determining whether his ambitions and Liverpool's plans continue to align.

articles.title: Bayern coach Vincent Kompany returns to club for first time since collapse
articles.summary: MUNICH (AP) — Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club’s training ground on Tuesday for the first time since he collapsed during practice las...
articles.body:
MUNICH (AP) — Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club's training ground on Tuesday for the first time since he collapsed during practice last month.

The 40-year-old Kompany had medical appointments at the Säbener Street complex, Kicker magazine reported, as he took another step toward his planned return after the international break.

Bayern had no team training on Tuesday with most of the players away. The team's next game is at home to Cologne in the Bundesliga on Nov. 20.

Bayern powerbroker Uli Hoeneß said on Sunday that Kompany would return in time for that match.

Kompany collapsed while observing a training session on Oct. 23 and was hospitalized for meningeal irritation, an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord. He had been dealing with a viral infection and hip injury.

Assistant Aaron Danks took charge of the team while Kompany was away and oversaw wins against Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atlético Madrid and Mainz with the only blot a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund in der Klassiker on Oct. 31.

articles.title: Penalty Tracker: Repetitive issues plague Texas against Missouri
articles.summary: The same types of penalties continue to hurt the Horns.
articles.body:
Against the Missouri Tigers, the Texas Longhorns continued to shoot themselves in the foot in the same fashion as previous contests despite the 34-20 victory in Columbia — pre-snap penalties on the offense, holding calls, and defensive mistakes continue to plague the Longhorns week after week, and Saturday was no different.

In total, Texas was called for seven penalties that netted 65 yards. They were also flagged for illegal formation and holding penalties that were both declined.

Including those two declined penalties, the Longhorn offense was called for three pre-snap penalties and two holding calls.

Once again, mental miscues cost Texas before the ball was even snapped.

The most costly false start was undoubtedly on 3rd and 5 with a little over two minutes to remaining in the fourth quarter as the Longhorns tried to execute their four-minute offense to ice the game. With a chance to face a manageable third-down situation, tight end Michael Masunas was flagged, creating third and long.

The penalty effectively ensured Missouri would get the ball back with a chance to drive down the field and tie the game. Indeed, Michael Terry III ran for six yards and Texas punted the ball away.

Though only one was accepted, the Longhorns were flagged for two holding calls. Tight end Emaree Watson and offensive lineman Brandon Baker were the culprits. Baker also contributed a false start.

Texas has now been flagged 10 times for holding, not including those that were declined, which is tied with false starts for the most frequent penalty against the Longhorn this season.

On the other side of the ball, penalties once again contributed to points. Of Missouri's 20 points, 10 came via drives that Texas was called for a penalty.

The opening drive granted the Tigers 30 free yards — 15 from a hands to the face penalty and another from defensive pass interference. The damage from the hands to the face penalty was exacerbated by the fact that it came on a play that produced a 15-yard reception, resulting in the Tigers gaining 30 yards on the play. Missouri went on to score a touchdown.

The hands to the face call went against defensive end Lance Jackson, who is tied for the most penalties on the team with five.

The defensive pass interference was called against cornerback Warren Roberson and was the ninth flagged against the Longhorns this season.

The other defensive penalty, a face mask by Ian Geffrard, helped the Tigers convert a field goal, so all 10 points scored by Missouri in the first half came on drives aided by Texas penalties.

False starts, holdings, and pass interference make up 48.4 percent of all accepted penalties against the Horns. Every week, some combination of these three penalties hurts Texas.

A year ago, the Longhorns averaged 8.3 penalties per game, totaling 108 flags for 906 yards over 13 games, which ranked 134th out of 136 teams in total penalties and 132nd in penalty yards per game.

This season, Texas is 80th in penalties per game at 6.67 and 99th in penalty yards per game with 63.0.

articles.title: Panthers create more cap space before today's trade deadline
articles.summary: Per Spotrac, the Panthers have created a bit of cap space after adjusting OT Taylor Moton's contract. Could a trade be in the works for today?
articles.body:
Could the Carolina Panthers be gearing up for a trade before today's deadline?

According to Spotrac, right tackle Taylor Moton has had $5.3 million of his salary converted into a signing bonus—freeing up $3.5 million in cap space for this season. The move, per Michael Ginnitti, was processed on Friday.

The timing and nature of this adjustment may indicate that the Panthers are angling to add some outside help via trade. Carolina previously had less than $1 million of salary cap space—which, obviously, wouldn't have been enough to accommodate a difference-making deal.

Head coach Dave Canales, who told reporters that the team is " open" to getting something done , acknowledged as much last week.

"Yeah, those are all the things to consider as far as what can be done," Canales stated. "So, again, until something gets real—my job is to evaluate the people that they put in front of me."

Teams have until 4 p.m. ET to complete any potential trades.

articles.title: Future Hogs Week 10: College football players who could help Commanders
articles.summary: Scouting college prospects for the Washington Commanders in upcoming NFL drafts
articles.body:
Week 10 of college football was loaded with meaningful games that could go a long way to impacting the College Football Playoff. We have to start with No. 1 Miami. They were down their best playmaker, Malachi Toney, and it showed most of the game. No. 11 Notre Dame took an early lead they never relinquished. Notre Dame should move up from No. 11 in the Playoff Rankings while Miami will certainly fall. The Holy War between No. 3 Utah and No. 9 BYU was competitive early, but the Utes shut out the Cougars in the second half to get the win.

In the SEC, No. 2 Georgia blew out No. 10 Ole Miss on the strength of quarterback Gunner Stockton's five touchdowns. No. 13 Tennessee leaned on their defense to end No. 6 Kentucky's hot streak. No. 5 Alabama went into Baton Rouge and won comfortably over No. 14 LSU. In the Big Ten, No. 8 UCLA remains undefeated after beating Minnesota. With the hopes of the playoffs hanging in the balance for both teams, No. 23 Oregon got the better of No. 12 Ohio State.

There will be a few interesting matchups in Week 11. After beating Ohio State, USC will travel to Bloomington to face Indiana. Georgia will look to stay on top of the SEC against Missouri, while LSU will try to keep their playoff hopes alive against Texas. Utah will try to remain undefeated against a dangerous Arizona team. Miami will have their hands full against Duke, a team with excellent young talent.

Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you:

Caden Veltkamp | QB | Senior | Florida Atlantic

He might not play for a Power Four school, but Caden Veltkamp should get more attention. He's a big, mobile quarterback at 6'5", 236 pounds. He's thrown for almost 3,000 yards, 27 touchdowns, and only five interceptions. Veltkamp can stand tall in the pocket, work through his progressions, and deliver accurate passes. He can vary his passes by putting pace on throws or putting air under them so receivers can run under them. He is mobile enough to navigate the pocket or run for positive yardage, but he usually keeps his eyes downfield to make plays. Veltkamp might be a riser once the draft process starts, but he would make a good developmental prospect. Veltkamp completed 17 of 25 attempts for 210 yards and four touchdowns in the Owls win over UTSA.

Boise State has put countless running backs into the league. Dylan Riley is next up. The junior is not a big back at 5'10", 203 pounds, but he is incredibly talented. Riley has plenty of burst to and through the line of scrimmage. For his size, he's strong and able to maintain his balance through contact. The speed is evident once he gets in the open field. Riley can play in either a zone or gap scheme, but I think he'll thrive with a team that primarily runs zone. In the passing game, Riley can do more than handle checkdown duties. He'll get open downfield as well as take short passes for long gains. In a win over Colorado State, Riley ran for 192 yards and two touchdowns on 19 attempts and caught two passes for 88 yards and a touchdown.

Illinois got a win against Nebraska and Collin Dixon was a big part of that win. Dixon already has broken the Illini record for most receiving touchdowns in a season with 12. Dixon is 6'1", 215 pounds, and plays like a strong receiver. If there is press man coverage or contact throughout the route, Dixon isn't phased by it. At the catch point, Dixon has great concentration and strong hands to make difficult, contested catches. The speed looks sufficient to play at the next level, but I'd like to see a little more route diversity and less plays to scheme him open. Dixon had eight receptions for 129 yards and two touchdowns against the Cornhuskers.

Wisconsin has quietly put together a nice season where they have the same record as Oregon and Ohio State. One reason has been the play of Jacob Harris . He's an athletic tight end, surprising given he is 6'6", 265 pounds. Harris has made several acrobatic catches this season. You can't expect him to be the fastest tight end at that size, but he gets open with good route running. After he gets the ball in his hands, Harris can be hard to bring down. As a blocker, he holds his ground against defenders. However, he needs to improve his ability to stay attached to defenders, especially in the run game. Harris caught two passes for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Badgers win over Rutgers.

How does Iowa keep producing quality offensive line prospects? Trevor Lauck is the Hawkeyes' left tackle, but he might be better suited to play guard in the NFL. Lauck has NFL size at 6'5", 315 pounds, and he can move well at that size. He is an aggressive blocker who doesn't want to block his assignments as much as bury them in the ground. Lauck generates movement in the run game, easily works to the second level, and tries to obliterate whomever gets in his way. He is solid in pass protection, but might struggle with speed around the edge because he lacks great foot speed and arm length. Lauck helped Iowa defeat Northwestern by giving up only one pressure and paving the way for 170 rushing yards.

Yhonzae Pierre | EDGE | Senior | Alabama

Alabama's defense has carried the Crimson Tide in several games. Their edge rusher Yhonzae Pierre deserves a little attention. He looks the part at 6'4", 251 pounds, with long arms. Pierre's calling card is his ability to convert speed to power and bull rush blockers. He can also use his quickness to beat blockers around the edge. What Pierre needs to improve is his hand usage. His hands need to land more cleanly on blockers to make the most of both his length and power. He also needs to develop counter moves when his initial rush stalls. Pierre has shown an ability to be effective dropping into coverage when asked to do so. Pierre had three tackles and a sack in the win over LSU.

Kentucky's offense could do nothing against Tennessee's defense. Arion Carter was all over the field for the Volunteers. The tape Carter produced against the Wildcats showed all facets of him as a prospect. On the sidelines, he was a vocal leader pumping up his team. Pre-snap, there were times Carter's preparation allowed him to know what plays were coming and to stop them. Carter, at 6'1", 238 pounds, uses his quickness to dart under blocks and close on ball carriers in an instant. Don't let the quickness fool you, Carter also will take on a lead blocker, shed him, and make the tackle. He looks good dropping into man coverage, but I need to see more of this aspect of his game. Carter had 13 tackles, four for a loss, and two sacks against Kentucky.

UCLA is on top of the Big Ten and remains undefeated after defeating Minnesota. One of the reasons for the turnaround has been Scooter Jackson . In his second year with the Bruins, after two years at Utah Tech, Jackson has improved his play. He has shown to be versatile enough to play both man and zone coverage, but UCLA often plays him in man. Jackson has good acceleration, quickness, and speed. If he's in off-man coverage, Jackson can trigger downhill and make a play on the ball with the hands to take it away. His speed allows him to follow defenders across the field, deep downfield, or get back into a play if beat. With a history of playing nickel, Jackson might offer a team inside out versatility. At 5'11", 191 pounds, I'd like to see him be more physical in coverage and as a tackler. Against Minnesota, Jackson had five tackles, two PBUs, and an interception.

Luke Talich had fantastic game against Miami and was a huge part of their win over Miami. Talich is a walk-on who is making the most of his opportunity. Talich is a big safety at 6'4", 222 pounds, but he moves like a smaller safety. Notre Dame played him deep and at the line of scrimmage. When he played deep, he not only prevented intermediate and deep throws, but was effective stopping the run from depth. At his size, taking on blockers, disengaging, and making tackles is not a problem. He has good change of direction at his size and was efficient in man coverage against a very good tight end for Miami, Elija Lofton. Talich sealed the game with a PBU to go along with six tackles, a forced fumble, and an interception.

articles.title: David Bednar and Opportunity Cost
articles.summary: The qualifying offer would make David Bednar the game’s highest paid reliever…and that’s where it should end.
articles.body:
Edwin Diaz makes $23 million a year to close out games for the Los Angeles Dodgers, a team that has seemed to stop caring about a payroll budget at all. This year's qualifying offer is $23.15 million, meaning if Yankee closer David Bednar accepts the one-time, one-year deal, he'll be the highest paid closer in baseball for one season, a season in which we're not quite sure what the baseball landscape will look like.

Of course Bednar has the right to negotiate a longer-term deal with the Yankees or any other team after declining the QO, and something like the three-year $51 million contract Devin Williams inked with the Mets might be more in line with what he wants —less money per year, but more of a long-term commitment especially if 2027 sees games be lost.

The Yankees were burned by the qualifying offer last year, extending it to Trent Grisham only for the alleged centerfielder fail to reach a full win of value, and the club was clearly worried about a similar misfire should they put the QO tab on Jazz Chisholm Jr. I think there's considerably less risk in having Bednar around, even at a slight annual overpay, than either of those two guys, but there's also less risk with an accepted QO than there is with signing him for more than one more year.

Let's start with the good — a 2.47 ERA that dropped to a 2.15 in the second half, Bednar brings a very old school, bulldog-like mentality to the ninth, seems to be eager to get the ball in the pressure moments, and makes me feel relaxed when he's on the mound with a two-run lead.

But the Yankee ability to pick up a turnip and turn it into a middle reliever with a 98 mph sinker and 2.61 ERA, which they do at least once a year, keeps expenses on relief pitching low. The team committed just $24,840,763 to the bullpen this year, a million bucks and change more than the Dodgers paid for Diaz alone while putting together a better unit albeit by ERA. The one team with a better relief ERA, the Red Sox, spent more than half of that (let's round up) $25 million on Aroldis Chapman, who had an excellent season, but the Yankees could recreate the proverbial aggregate for less money.

As always, I don't care about Hal Steinbrenner's wallet, but he does, and that kind of flexibility in filling out a bullpen gives the Yankees a wide range of options — they are almost always able to make deals at the trade deadline because they have a little extra money that they DIDN'T give to someone like Aroldis Chapman or Edwin Diaz or Josh Hader, or they can give that extra money to a headlining free agent, or they can buck their fungible relief trend and have Bednar for one expensive year.

At one year I don't mind ballooning the relief budget, especially when the free agent class is pretty underwhelming. I don't think the Yankees will make a push for Tarik Skubal, Jazz can go play somewhere else, and while I want Teruaki Sato, I don't imagine I'd consider Brian Cashman a failure if he can't sign the NPB MVP. At three or four years, I no longer want Bednar — his fastball was down a full mile per hour in 2026, and while I don't mind a 33-year-old closer, I worry a lot about a 34 or 35 year old.

That kind of commitment also restricts the pot of money that can be given out in the 2028 or 2029 FA classes, both stronger than the '27 cohort. Lastly, I think a multi-year deal to closers locks them in a role because of the money they're owed; the closer is the closer because he's the closer. Relief pitching is exactly where you want to maintain your flexibility, one year with David Bednar sounds like a great time. Much more than that locks up resources in the side of the roster the Yankees are best at tinkering with.

articles.title: Nebraska’s Matt Rhule Faces $60 Million Buyout As Season Crumbles
articles.summary: Matt Rhule fires Dana Holgorsen after a 24-13 loss to Illinois. With a $60 million buyout, can Nebraska fix a team that went from 5-0 to 5-4?
articles.body:
Matt Rhule fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen on Saturday afternoon, according to Yahoo Sports . The move comes right after Nebraska lost 24-13 to Illinois on Friday night. This loss marks the fourth straight defeat for the Cornhuskers. The team started the season with a perfect 5-0 record. Now they sit at 5-4 and cannot score enough points to win. For the remainder of the season, Glenn Thomas will assume responsibility for play-calling. He is the co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach. Rhule acknowledged that the offensive strategy and its execution are failing. He took full blame for the results in a statement released to the public.

Nebraska made a risky bet on Rhule a year ago. The school extended his contract through 2032 after Penn State fired James Franklin. This agreement burdens the university with a buyout near the $60 million mark. Rhule has ties to Penn State, having gone to high school in State College. The athletic director, Pat Kraft, worked with him at Temple. Nebraska felt the program was on the right track at the time. They wanted to avoid a long coach search. Now that decision looks like a huge mistake. The school is stuck with a coach who has a record of 24-23. Angry supporters are discovering fresh methods to express their dismay at the program. The sellout streak that began in 1962 could finally end. A fan base enduring numerous losing streaks across the past few decades faces these dark times.

The hiring of Holgorsen was a square peg in a round hole. That style was never a great fit in the Big Ten. Rhule hired him anyway. The plan shifted when quarterback Dylan Raiola transferred to Oregon. The team then built an offense around Anthony Colandrea. Colandrea has a lot of running ability. Nebraska declared a week or so ago that Colandrea committed to a fifth year in 2027. Then they fired Holgorsen. The next offensive coordinator will need to work around the current quarterback. Rushing yardage places the offense among the Big Ten leaders. Yet the team still loses close games. During the four-game slump, the Cornhuskers averaged only 13.5 points per contest. An average of 19.5 points was surrendered by the defense over the past four games. But they could not finish drives or put the ball in the end zone.

Rhule pledged further adjustments to aid the team in securing victories. He stated his intent to keep assessing the program as the season progresses. The firing of Holgorsen is just the first step. The path forward appears difficult for the games that remain. Next week, Nebraska travels to face the Rutgers Scarlet Knights. Ranked home contests versus Ohio State follow on the schedule. A concluding away game versus the Iowa Hawkeyes comes after that. Four consecutive victories helped Illinois regain its composure. Losses to Indiana, Oregon, Washington, and Illinois were part of the skid that saw Nebraska crash. Turning things around remains the determination of the entire program. But the math is simple. To end the season strongly, the team requires a spark. The next game is on the road against Rutgers next week.

articles.title: Panthers earn decent grade in Week 9 despite crushing loss to Broncos
articles.summary: CBS Sports credited the Panthers for sticking to the Broncos in Week 9, even despite the loss.
articles.body:
There are no moral victories in the NFL. That said, it's definitely better to lose by one score to a contender than to get blown out by a bad team.

The Carolina Panthers have done both this season. Right now, however, they're fresh off doing the former.

In Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Denver Broncos , the Panthers had several chances to take control of the game—but penalties, defensive miscues, bad luck and some questionable officiating ultimately made that impossible.

For their efforts Carolina has gotten a respectable 'B-' grade from John Breech at CBS Sports this week. Breech writes:

The Panthers offense was firing on all cylinders: Chuba Hubbard averaged nearly 5 yards per carry and five different players caught at least four passes. The problem for the Panthers is that there were just too many mistakes ranging from a soul-crushing fumble by [Bryce] Young in the fourth quarter to a bizarre interception to a missed field goal. The Panthers just kept shooting themselves in the foot. You can't make those mistakes if you want to beat good teams, and the Broncos are a good team.

Carolina finished the day having out-gained Denver 353 yards to 312. Young was also strong against a very formidable defense, completing 28 of his 39 throws for 276 yards, three scores and a pick.

Looking ahead, the Panthers have to consider themselves desperate and hungry—and the next three games on their schedule should be highly-winnable matchups. If they can take care of business against the New Orleans Saints , a Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens team, and get some revenge on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , they'll be over .500 going into December.

articles.title: Colorado vs. Houston football series history, all-time record
articles.summary: Colorado and Houston enter Friday's game tied 1-1 in their series, with the Cougars making their first-ever visit to Folsom Field.
articles.body:
Colorado will host Houston for the first time Friday, adding a Boulder chapter to the series that began nearly 55 years ago.

The Buffaloes and Cougars are tied 1-1 all-time after Houston won last season's matchup 36-20. Their only previous meeting came in the 1971 Astro-Bluebonnet Bowl, which Colorado won 29-17.

Friday's game at Folsom Field will be their third meeting overall and second as Big 12 opponents. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. MT.

Colorado won the first meeting in a bowl game

The Buffaloes defeated Houston 29-17 on Dec. 31, 1971, at the Astrodome in the Astro-Bluebonnet Bowl.

Running back Charlie Davis rushed for 202 yards on 37 carries and earned bowl MVP honors. Colorado scored 16 points in the second quarter and held off the Cougars to complete a 10-2 season under coach Eddie Crowder.

The programs then went more than five decades without another meeting.

The Cougars won 36-20 in Houston last season on Sept. 12, 2025, taking theteams'' first regular-season meeting and first conference matchup.

Colorado trailed 16-14 at halftime before Houston outscored the Buffaloes 20-6 over the final two quarters. The 16-point victory remains the largest margin in the brief series.

Colorado enters Friday with a 3-6 record after their 20-10 loss to Arizona State , and a 1-1 record all-time against Houston. The Buffaloes will try to take their first home meeting and reclaim the series lead after theCougars'' victory last September.

articles.title: Texas freshmen report: Marcus Spears Jr., Austin Goosby accompanied by 3rd young star
articles.summary: Texas' highly prized recruit wasn't the only freshman to shine in the Longhorns latest blowout victory on Monday.
articles.body:
Marcus Spears Jr. will be tested sooner than later as a 17-year-old freshman. But the Texas men's basketball forward has yet to meet his match through three college games to date.

Spears, a five-star recruit for the class of 2026, totaled 24 points and posted a plus-49 in a pair of blowout wins over small-conference opponents last week. Monday continued the early season pattern. Spears played just 20 minutes in a 93-62 win over Grambling State . He still tallied 12 points, four rebounds and two assists in that span, and Texas outscored Grambling State by 15 points in his time on the floor.

The 6-foot-7 North Texas native was efficient against Grambling State. His film was smooth and refined for a player who won't turn 18 until the completion of the 2026-27 season. Spears shook past a Tigers defender with a drop step and subsequent layup midway through the second half. He immediately recognized an incoming double team minutes earlier, then pinged the ball to fellow frehsman Austin Goosby for a 3-pointer.

Spears added one highlight-reel dunk for the Moody Center crowd Monday night. He skied to the rim for an alley-oop dunk late in the first half, one that was impressive, though perhaps not as electric as the dunk-contest worthy show he put on pregame.

Marcus Spears Jr. overshadowed by sharpshooter

Spears shined in an efficient, effective and above-the-rim effort Monday. He also wasn't the flashiest freshman on the floor.

First-year guard Joe Sterling brought the greatest buzz out of a sleepy crowd with his three 3-pointers, two of which he canned in the game's first eight minutes. Sterling is an elite shooter. His free-throw performance during summer workouts in Austin drew national attention. Those around Texas' program call him (a bit facetiously) "Joe Curry." Sterling lived up to his nickname with a 10 made threes in his first three collegiate games

Sterling is a 6-foot-4 sharpshooter who commands major defensive attention. He earned praise from his coach postgame for his work on the other end of the floor.

"Joe is one of those guys that, he's just smart. And he has a knack for being in the right place," Texas head coach Sean Miller said postgame. "We keep steals and deflections (stats) every day in practice, in games, scrimmages, and he's actually near the top. You may not think that, but he's deceptive with his size and he has great instincts.

"He's been more than a pleasant surprise. We believed in him, that's why we brought him to Texas. His maturity, his ability to make shots, and again, do the other things around making shots that make him a solid player, he's really off to a great start for us."

Miller will continue to play Sterling if he pairs strong shooting with passable defense. That could cost another freshman playing time in Texas' rotation.

Bo Ogden is a fellow reserve guard for the Longhorns, an Austin Westlake product who committed to Texas in 2025 as a four-star recruit. The Longhorns' starting five is secure at the moment, with Goosby and Spears joined by three upper classmen. Goosby, a guard, leads the team in minutes (73), assists (13) and steals (seven) through three games.

If Sterling were to struggle, Ogden would likely seize his minutes, becoming Texas' primary guard off the bench. But that wasn't the case through three games, with Sterling cooking early while Ogden has a combined 16 points in 46 minutes across the last three games. Expect Sterling and Ogden to continue to jockey for minutes, with plenty of time for Miller to sort out his rotation.

That sooner-than-later test for Spears? How about Sunday, when Texas will face Baylor at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio.

Baylor isn't ranked as of Monday. Its also a program that's 2-0 this season, one with expectation of reaching the NCAA Tournament in March. Texas isn't totally done with the cupcake portion of its schedule. But a bigger challenge is on the immediate horizon, the best test yet for the Longhorns' collection of freshmen.

articles.title: Week 11 college football prediction market picks: Wake Forest, Utah lead Kalshi, Polymarket
articles.summary: Undefeated Utah visits Noah Fifita and Arizona, while Wake Forest expects quarterback Gio Lopez back for an ACC title-race trip to SMU.
articles.body:
College football 's prediction market in this Week 11 slate takes undefeated Utah to Tucson to face Noah Fifita and Arizona , puts Tennessee in front of a blackout crowd at Kyle Field and sends Wake Forest to SMU with ACC title stakes.

Five of the six picks side with the market favorite, though Wake Forest at 51% is close to a coin flip. The exception is Cincinnati, which travels to Ames as an outright upset pick against Iowa State.

Wake Forest has won six straight since its only loss to Miami, and quarterback Gio Lopez should return after sitting out Saturday's 77-0 win over Merrimack with a leg injury. Coach Jake Dickert said Monday, "He'll be ready to go Saturday ." Lopez has thrown 18 touchdowns against one interception this season.

SMU scored on its first eight drives in a 51-28 win over Virginia Tech , and Kevin Jennings threw for 350 yards and four touchdowns. Still, the Mustangs allow 5.25 yards per carry, so Wake Forest can lean on its running game and keep Jennings on the sideline. The Demon Deacons also won last year's meeting 13-12.

Pick: 34-27, Wake Forest (Wake Forest -1.5, Under 61.5)

Cincinnati rallied from 14 points down at Houston before a 51-yard touchdown run with 5:10 left and a backward-pass ruling on its final drive sealed a 31-24 loss . Running back Cole Tabb, who has 752 rushing yards, left after a hard hit, but the Enquirer reported he appeared fine afterward.

Iowa State has allowed at least 42 points in back-to-back games, and coach Jimmy Rogers said the Baylor loss "really comes down to poor execution in so many ways ." The Cyclones give up 5.73 yards per carry. Aiden Flora's 1,119 rushing yards keep Iowa State dangerous, but Cincinnati's ground game should win a shootout in Ames.

Pick: 34-31, Cincinnati (Cincinnati +3, Over 60.5)

Tennessee's defense carried a 34-6 win over Kentucky , as linebacker Arion Carter posted two sacks and four tackles for loss. The offense was quieter. Quarterback George MacIntyre threw for 125 yards, and the Vols had 13 points through three quarters. Running back DeSean Bishop and his 1,075 rushing yards give them a dependable fallback.

Texas A&M has scored 20 points or fewer in three of its last four games, including a 17-9 loss at South Carolina, and Marcel Reed has seven touchdown passes all season. The Aggies will have an Operation Blackout crowd behind them, but Tennessee's defense, which creates havoc on 21.3% of plays, decides a low-scoring game.

Pick: 24-17, Tennessee (Tennessee -2.5, Under 43.5)

Louisville ran for 251 yards in a 44-17 win at Georgia Tech, its fourth straight victory. Coach Jeff Brohm, who earned his 100th career win, said winning four in a row " after starting 2-3 is a testament to our guys and coaches ." The Cardinals have scored at least 27 points in all nine games.

North Carolina is one win from bowl eligibility after a 38-21 win at UConn, where quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. threw three touchdowns. But the Tar Heels needed three takeaways to pull away from a .500 team. Lincoln Kienholz, who led Louisville with 81 rushing yards last week, and running back Isaac Brown give the Cardinals the stronger ground game in Chapel Hill.

Pick: 34-27, Louisville (Louisville -3.5, Over 59.5)

Utah is 9-0 and No. 2 in the AP poll after intercepting BYU's Bear Bachmeier four times in a 28-20 win. Quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four touchdowns, and coach Morgan Scalley said running back Wayshawn Parker's heel injury shouldn't be an issue in Tucson.

Arizona hasn't lost at home and has won the last two meetings . Scalley admitted " Noah Fifita's had our number for the last two times that we've played him." Fifita threw for 313 yards to rally the Wildcats past TCU 29-28. Utah's secondary just picked off four passes against a top-10 opponent, and that defense keeps the Utes unbeaten.

Pick: 31-24, Utah (Utah -2.5, Over 54.5)

North Texas is the only team still unbeaten in American Conference play after a 52-23 win over Rice , its sixth straight victory. Running back Jahiem White ran for 139 yards and three touchdowns and has 1,186 rushing yards this season. The Mean Green rank fifth nationally in adjusted expected points added per play on offense.

UTSA lost 60-29 at Florida Atlantic and allowed 563 yards, and coach Jeff Traylor said his staff was " totally outcoached ." North Texas allows 7.61 yards per dropback, so Owen McCown can keep this close on homecoming night at the Alamodome. Still, the Mean Green won last year's meeting 55-17 and have the offense to win a shootout.

Pick: 41-34, North Texas (North Texas -2.5, Under 77.5)
